75b125470572d889: DUBLIN: Ireland coach Andy Farrell said he was delighted "to get a good win" after his side routed Argentina 42-12 in their Nations Championship Test at Lansdowne Road but added they could have been "more ruthless."
Hugo Keenan led the way scoring a hat-trick of tries – in his first home Test in over a year – as the Irish ran in six tries against a disappointing Pumas outfit.
The Irish go on to host Fiji on Saturday week before the biggest challenge of all world champions South Africa in a fortnight – prior to finals weekend at Twickenham.
"Well, first and foremost delighted to get the win and a good win at that," said Farrell.
"You know, six tries to two says a lot.
"So delighted to get the season off with a big W."

Farrell had said in the lead-up to the match he felt the Irish in their present state were not contenders to win next year's Rugby World Cup – a tournament they have yet to even reach the semi-finals.
The 51-year-old Englishman, who arguably with a stronger team guided them to the 2023 quarter-finals, did not repeat that after Friday's Test but he said there were things they needed to work on.
"How we can be a little bit more ruthless because that's the team that we want to be," he said.
Farrell, though, said all in all "it's a good place to be."
His Argentina counterpart Felipe Contepomi has had little time with his players and he said it showed in the differences between the two teams.
"Well, to start with, 30 points, and then obviously I think there was a more cohesive and slick team, the Irish, and we made a lot of individual errors," said the 49-year-old.
"I'm very proud for the boys. The way they pushed, they tried, and they came out and kept running.
"But it's tough when you defend too much against a team that is is very good with ball in hand."
- 'Great starting point' -
Contepomi's side go on to play Italy and then Six Nations champions France in what has been a tough year in terms of results.
However, he took some positives out of the match.
"Well, the initiative, how they went out straight off the blocks and then there was some good rugby," said Contepomi.
"The attitude. I think the players they were fantastic, the way we got together in four days, put up a performance in a test match against the third placed team in the world."
Keenan may have taken the man of the match award and the back slapping from his team-mates but the 30-year-old fullback is never one to blow his own trumpet.
"It was at the end of a few good plays, to be honest," he said of his three tries.
"Three walk-ins, I think.

"So I'll take any to be honest, but we got a bonus point playing against a really tough Argentinian side, to beat them by 30 points and probably not play to our full potential is exciting because there's a lot to work on."
His teammate Tadhg Beirne said "it was a great starting point" but like Farrell and Keenan saw plenty of room for improvement.

"I think we were very good in patches, and I think some of the tries we scored were proper team tries, which will be probably the most pleasing part about it," said Beirne, who will be 35 when the World Cup comes round.

"But I think we'll probably be walking away from that game with the feeling we could have gotten a lot more out of it in terms of scores, so there was some good parts for sure, but there was certainly a lot of parts that need to be better." - AFP

9dad6640fb13dba1: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — Two vessels and other items with an estimated total value of RM8 million were seized by the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) in Penang waters on Thursday for allegedly carrying out cargo transfer activities without a valid licence.

In a statement today, Penang MMEA director Maritime Captain Muhammad Suffi Mohd Ramli said the vessels, a tugboat and an unregistered sampan, were detained at 11.40am following information received and public complaints.

He said an initial inspection found that the vessels were allegedly involved in transferring cargo from the sampan to the tugboat without a valid cargo licence as required under the Merchant Shipping Ordinance (MSO) 1952.

Those detained comprised two Vietnamese nationals, who were the tugboat’s master and chief engineer, and a local man who was the sampan skipper, along with the vessels, related documents and other seized items, all of which were handed over to MMEA investigating officers for further investigation.

Muhammad Suffi said compliance with maritime laws and licensing conditions was essential to ensuring navigational safety, orderly shipping activities and the protection of national interests. — Bernama
c2f35984a320a1aa: WASHINGTON, Nov 7 — Known for his sharp suits, sunglasses and menacing air, Stephen Miller has long been one of US President Donald Trump’s most loyal and combative consiglieres.
Now Trump has named the architect of his immigration crackdown as his chief of staff — the clearest possible signal that the gloves are off after the US midterms.
Miller, 41, said Friday he was ready for battle.
“The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our President and defend this magnificent Republic,” Miller said on X.
His appointment fired up a MAGA movement stunned by the Republican hammering in the midterms.
“IT’S MILLER TIME,” former congressman Matt Gaetz said, quoting, like many other allies, a famous US beer commercial.
Democrats were not so thrilled.
“Stephen Miller is a dangerous xenophobe and reckless extremist who has American blood on his hands,” incoming House Majority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said.
Dubbed Trump’s “brain,” Miller has been the most ideological presence in the president’s inner circle since he started working for him in 2016.
Miller frequently echoes far-right talking points about Western civilization being under threat from an “invasion” of migrants — and under Trump he has translated that into policy.
‘He gets it’
It was Miller, whose official job title is currently deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security advisor, who was behind the mass deportations in Trump’s second term.
Reports said Miller pushed Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to drastically step up their deportations after levels under Trump fell below those of the Biden administration.

For Democrats, Stephen Miller is the symbol of the excesses of Trump’s immigration policy, from the masked agents rounding up undocumented migrants, to the shootings by federal agents that left two Americans dead.
His management style is reportedly equally hardline.
In their book “Regime Change,” New York Times journalists Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan said Miller was a domineering boss who regularly berated staff members.

Miller would also present his views as requests from the president — but was cautious about expressing his opinions in front of Trump himself, and was careful not to leave a paper trail, they reported.
In the early months of Trump’s second presidency Miller was often a combative presence in front of the cameras on the White House driveway.
But after the outrage over shootings of Alex Pretti and Renee Good by immigration agents in Minneapolis in January prompted the White House to roll back the policy, he has kept a lower profile.

First Lady Melania Trump even complained to President Trump that some of her friends were being swept up in the crackdown, prompting Trump to tell aides Miller had gone “too far,” the Wall Street Journal reported this week.
Now, however, he has risen further than ever.
“Stephen’s been with me from the beginning,” Trump told reporters on Friday “He gets it.”
Wife stokes Greenland row
Born in liberal Santa Monica in Los Angeles, Miller joined as a speechwriter just before the start of Trump’s first term — and in that time his hardline stance made him something of an outlier.
The young firebrand was one of the designs of the so-called “Muslim travel bans” in Trump’s first presidency, which later ran into legal difficulties after they were poorly drafted.
Miller however largely avoided the chaotic feuding that engulfed Trump’s first White House.
And he stuck by his boss even as Trump’s first term ended in the disgrace of the US Capitol attack on January 6, 2021.
His wife Katie is also a prominent figure in Trumpworld.
She was the spokeswoman for Elon Musk’s ill-fated Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) and has since carved out as an influencer in the MAGA and “tradwife” movements.

Most notoriously, she also fanned Trump’s claims over Greenland by posting a picture of the island overlaid by the American flag and the word “soon,” shortly after Trump’s military operation in Venezuela. — AFP
3dc8fa623ddbca4b: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Ghosts and spirits have long been staples of horror films, but sometimes the most unsettling horrors come not from the supernatural, but from the cruelty people inflict on one another.
This is the central idea behind The Confessions of a Shaman.

This Thai horror-thriller directed by Natthanon Cholumpi explores grief, injustice and desperation through a story involving black magic while examining how personal suffering can drive people toward disturbing choices.
Thai horror cinema has long drawn inspiration from folklore, spiritual beliefs and occult traditions.
The Confessions of a Shaman uses these familiar elements as a backdrop to explore human suffering and the increasingly blurred boundaries between victim and perpetrator.
At the centre of the story is Tor, played by Teeradetch Metawarayut, whose life takes a devastating turn following a series of injustices.
Overwhelmed by grief, Tor turns to black magic in search of retribution, setting him on a path shaped by anger and increasingly disturbing choices.
Rather than relying solely on supernatural encounters to create fear, the film examines what drives Tor’s transformation, showing how personal tragedy can push someone toward darkness.
A box-office hit with a chilling Malaysian debut
The film arrives in Malaysian cinemas with an impressive commercial performance in Thailand behind it.

Following its Thai theatrical release on August 12, 2026, The Confessions of a Shaman reportedly collected THB120 million (approximately RM14.47 million) within its first five days, making it the country’s second-highest-grossing Thai film of 2026 at the time.

The film is produced with the involvement of M Studio, the company associated with Thailand’s successful Death Whisperer franchise, which has established a strong following among fans of Thai supernatural horror.

Adding to its appeal, Thai K-pop star BamBam, best known as a member of internationally recognised boy group GOT7, makes his feature-film debut with the production, offering another point of interest for audiences familiar with his music career.

The Confessions of a Shaman is also adapted from a popular spooky story featured on The Ghost Radio, one of Thailand’s best-known horror storytelling channels on YouTube, which boasts millions of subscribers.
While The Confessions of a Shaman draws on familiar Thai horror elements, its exploration of grief, injustice and human cruelty gives the story a darker dimension beyond its supernatural premise.
Rather than presenting evil as something that exists only in the spirit world, the film suggests that the suffering people inflict on one another can be equally, if not more, terrifying.
Sometimes, the greatest horrors are not found among the dead, but created by the living.
The Confessions of a Shaman opens in Malaysian cinemas today, distributed by Barnstorm Entertainment, and also stars Shahkrit Yamnarm and Jelilcha Kapaun.
d433c10eaca84212: LONDON: England face Australia in the Nations Championship at Twickenham on Sunday in one of the most attractive clashes of the first round of November fixtures.
AFP Sport looks at three aspects surrounding an intriguing matchup between the old rivals:
England go all in on Borthwick
It is not unusual for coaches to be given a vote of confidence by their employers, but the Rugby Football Union have gone above and beyond with England boss Steve Borthwick.
This week RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney gave Borthwick his unequivocal backing to lead England at the 2027 World Cup.

Two months ago, the RFU extended Borthwick's contract until after the 2028 Six Nations, even though this year England lost four out of five matches in a single Championship for the first time in the tournament's history.
England have lost five of their last seven Tests, but Sweeney insisted: "We're committed to Steve. We believe in what he's doing.
"We had a difficult Six Nations this year, we accept that, but we just want to see continued progress and we're backing him to get that done."
Beale 'no passenger' despite absence v England
Kurtley Beale's long wait to return to Test action goes on after the veteran back was left out of Australia's match-day 23 to play England.
Beale was a surprise addition to Australia's touring squad after Hunter Paisami withdrew for personal reasons.
The 37-year-old has played 95 Tests but his last was in 2021.
"Well he's in the squad, so he was in the selection mix for sure," said Wallabies coach Les Kiss on Friday after naming his side to play England.

"Kurtley's totally aware that he is in the picture. He's not here as a passenger, that's for sure," added Kiss, who has selected Isaac Henry and Len Ikitau in midfield while keeping faith with Declan Meredith.
Contract dispute
Australia begin their European tour under the shadow of a pay row that threatens to cause a bitter dispute ahead of the World Cup on their home soil.

The Wallabies' two most recent Tests, where they conceded a combined 93 points in a pair of heavy defeats by New Zealand, were the last played under the previous collective bargaining agreement, struck between Rugby Australia and its players in 2023.
In April, RA declared "record operating surplus" of Aus $70 million (US $48 million) only two years on from posting an Aus $37 million deficit.
RA are set to receive a staging fee of some Aus $100 million from World Rugby for staging the 2027 World Cup.
But the underlying finances of Australian rugby remain precarious. They only get to host the Lions once every 12 years and it may be much longer before Australia stages another World Cup after 2027.
Australian male rugby union players are already paid considerably less than those in rugby league who play in the thriving NRL, the leading club competition in the 13-a-side code.
Kiss insisted the issue was not proving a distraction to his squad.
"All I know is that they're the right people in the room trying to find a solution, to find a win-win that can work and I'm just focused on getting the team right," he said.
"I've got to say the boys, they don't talk about it, they just focus on what the job is, which is pleasing." - AFP

f11189c6bbd6dd76: JAKARTA, Nov 7 — Efforts will be made to convene the Malaysia-Indonesia Annual Consultation at the earliest opportunity, with several memoranda of understanding (MoUs) already agreed upon for signing during the high-level meeting.

Malaysian Ambassador to Indonesia Datuk Muzafar Shah Mustafa said he had raised the matter directly with President Prabowo Subianto during an interaction at Istana Merdeka on Friday, following the presentation of his credentials to the Indonesian leader.
“Overall, I view President Prabowo’s remarks as very positive, and I hope this will provide further momentum to strengthen the good relations between Malaysia and Indonesia,” he told Bernama.
The upcoming 14th Annual Consultation will bring together Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Prabowo to review bilateral cooperation and discuss issues of mutual interest.

The Annual Consultation is the highest-level bilateral mechanism between the two countries, providing a platform for their leaders to advance cooperation in trade, investment, defence, security, border matters, and other strategic areas.
The previous consultation, the 13th in the series, was held in Jakarta on July 29, 2025, marking the revival of the mechanism after the last meeting in Kuching, Sarawak, in 2017.

Muzafar said he also conveyed greetings from the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, and Anwar to Prabowo, while reaffirming Malaysia’s commitment to strengthening cooperation with Indonesia as a neighbour and strategic partner.

“President Prabowo repeatedly emphasised that Malaysia and Indonesia are brotherly nations. He also spoke about his close relationship with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, whom he described as a former schoolmate, as well as his close ties with Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim,” he said.
The Indonesian President also emphasised the close cultural and people-to-people ties between the two countries and expressed hope that bilateral relations would continue to grow.
Malaysia and Indonesia will commemorate the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2027, marking seven decades of bilateral ties since the establishment of formal ties in 1957.

On forest and land fires, Muzafar said Prabowo emphasised that Indonesia had done its utmost to tackle the problem, including mobilising tens of thousands of personnel and deploying various firefighting assets.
He said Prabowo also referred to companies including those from Malaysia and Singapore, and stressed that firm action would be taken against those found to have committed offences. — Bernama
7e525aff4d22b7cc: ASUNCION: After three years as vice-president, it took just three days of crisis to catapult Pedro Alliana to Paraguay's presidency.
The former national basketball player, businessman, and ruling party insider was rapidly sworn in Friday, minutes after the impeachment of his former boss, Santiago Pena.
A lifelong party loyalist whose life has been marked by family tragedy, Alliana, 52, now finds himself leading Paraguay at a moment of acute political turmoil.
Earlier this week, Ueno Bank suddenly collapsed, freezing the savings of half of Paraguay's adult population.
On being sworn in Friday, Alliana pledged to put that right in the time he has before the term ends in August 2028.

Born on February 19, 1974, in the riverside city of Pilar, Allina emerged as a national political figure with the backing of former president Horacio Cartes -- still one of the country's most influential political operators and leader of the ruling Colorado Party.
Before entering politics, Allina built a career as a businessman and won recognition as a talented basketball player, earning a place on Paraguay's national team in 1991.
His life has also been marked by personal hardship.
Tragedy struck in 2003, when his brother Rodolfo "Pili" Alliana, 24, was kidnapped and murdered.
A court found that he was kidnapped to fund a cigarette smuggling operation -- a massive billion-dollar trade in the landlocked nation.
In 2018, he was diagnosed with leukemia and underwent treatment in Brazil.
A year later, he announced he had overcome the illness, although he had to undergo chemotherapy again in 2021.
Party operator
Politics was present in Alliana's life from an early age. His parents both served as local councilors.
But his first foray into politics ended in defeat in 2006, when he unsuccessfully sought the mayoralty of his hometown at age 32.
Two years later, however, he was elected governor of the southern department of Neembucu.
From there, he steadily climbed the political ladder. He served in the Chamber of Deputies from 2013 to 2023, presided over the lower house, then led the Colorado Party.
His rise accelerated through a faction founded by Cartes within the Colorado Party.
In 2021, he expected to run for the Senate, but later recalled that Cartes informed him he would instead become Pena's running mate.
Pena himself publicly praised his future deputy, saying Alliana could become "the best vice-president in Paraguay's history."

Married to congresswoman Fabiana Souto and father of four children, Alliana faced criticism over the number of relatives employed in public administration, including his eldest daughter, Montserrat Alliana.
Even so, political observers frequently viewed him as one of the figures best positioned to inherit leadership of the ruling party -- just not this quickly.
A year after taking office as vice-president, Alliana publicly acknowledged his ambition to one day take the highest office.
In 2025, Cartes openly encouraged those aspirations. "Pedro, you are blessed," the former president said during a party event, urging supporters to back him as the "next president of the Republic."
Yet, as had happened earlier with Pena, relations between Cartes and Alliana eventually cooled.

After the former president withdrew support for his presidential ambitions, Alliana publicly signaled his independence, declaring on October 26 that loyalty should not be confused with "blind obedience."
His fortunes changed again when lawmakers impeached Pena but rejected proceedings against Alliana, shelving the case against the vice-president.
86a2c596ef148bd9: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The 24th Deepavali Carnival at the National Stadium in Bukit Jalil near here, which attracted nearly 200,000 visitors, including foreign tourists, proves the event is not merely a festive shopping venue but also a platform to spur local businesses.

Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the encouraging response to the nine-day carnival, which began October 30, gave 700 entrepreneurs an opportunity to expand their market reach and boost sales.
He said that, based on his observation, business activities at participating stalls showed positive growth.
“Preparations have indeed been good. I visited the stalls here, and their sales have been very good. I understand that this is the 24th time this carnival has been held.

“Some visitors came from Medan, Singapore and Australia. Sometimes they come here just as tourists to visit Malaysia, but after attending this carnival, they return repeatedly,” he told reporters after visiting the carnival yesterday.
Ramanan said the government is also prepared to look into suitable support and assistance to empower entrepreneurs participating in the carnival.
The carnival gathered various exhibitors and local entrepreneurs offering goods, food, beverages and essential items for Deepavali. — Bernama
f2569ed935de3ac7: LOS ANGELES, Nov 7 — Voters in Washington state approved a measure barring transgender athletes from playing on girls sports teams, a major US midterms loss for LGBTQ advocates in the normally blue state.
With about 80 per cent of ballots counted Friday, approximately 57 per cent of voters approved the measure while 43 per cent opted against it, and opponents conceded defeat.
The initiative will require the prohibition of transgender girls from “competing with and against female students.”
Approval of the conservative measure in a state that normally votes Democratic stands in stark contrast to the otherwise disappointing November 3 midterm vote for Republicans.
Opponents of the measure included doctors who said that it is “not backed by clinical guidelines, and would create unwarranted stress and harm for young girls.”
Under the initiative girls who want to play sports must undergo a physical reproductive organ exam, or genetic and hormone testing.
More than half of states have enacted laws in recent years restricting the participation of transgender students in sports.
The US Supreme Court upheld state bans in June.
The measure in Washington state was considered among the most extreme of four total similar measures that passed in this week’s election.
The others were in Arizona, Nebraska and Colorado.
‘Fight is not over’
Trans athletes have been the target of Republican lawmakers and anti-LGBTQ groups who argue that their participation in girls and women’s sports is unfair.

The political action committee behind the measure, Let’s Go Washington – which is bankrolled by conservative hedge fund manager Brian Heywood – called its passage “a huge win for girls in Washington state.”
“Girls will compete without boys in their sports!” the group said on social media.
Civil rights advocates have countered that such efforts scapegoat a very small group of people, most of them children, who already face discrimination and bullying.
Over half of transgender youth have had suicidal thoughts in their lifetime and 31 per cent have made at least one suicide attempt, according to the American Academy of Pediatrics.

The Washington Interscholastic Activities Association, which governs school-linked youth sports in the northwestern state, said earlier this year it is aware of just 10 transgender middle and high schoolers who play sports, out of some 200,000 students competing statewide.

Libby Watson – campaign manager of the group No Hate WA State, which advocated against the Washington measure – cast the initiative as “deceptive” and a bid “by MAGA forces to target trans kids for their own political gain.”
The results are a “disappointment,” Watson said in a statement, but “the fight is not over.”
“To all trans girls participating in school sports in Washington, we want you to know that you belong: on the field, on the court, on the team,” the advocate continued.
“We stand with you and will continue to fight for a day when you can play sports without controversy.” — AFP
7ae498146df563d4: SIBU, Nov 7 — Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) Vice President Datuk Dr Annuar Rapaee has defended the Sarawak government’s inclusive policy of providing educational opportunities to all races, while reminding the Bumiputera community not to be left behind in seizing the opportunities provided.

He said the Bumiputera community should not question the opportunities given to other races, but should instead ensure that their children take advantage of the state government’s educational and development opportunities.
“What we need to worry about is not the opportunities opened to others. What we should worry about is whether our Bumiputera children are seizing those open opportunities.

“Do not worry at all that other communities are given opportunities because in Sarawak, every layer of society will be given opportunities as long as they have the appropriate qualifications,” he said when speaking at the Nangka Youth Friendly Dinner here last night.

The incumbent Nangka state assemblyman said that throughout his 15 years representing the area, he has adhered to the principle that no community should be sidelined from development regardless of their racial background.

Meanwhile, Dr Annuar acknowledged that not all public issues could be resolved throughout his tenure, but stressed that every trust given will continue to be carried out to the best of his ability. — Bernama

950c75d38839bb39: DOHA: Malaysia intends to propose at the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) level that Internet coverage measurements should no longer focus solely on the Coverage of Populated Areas (COPA) standard, but should also take into account areas where economic activities take place.

Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the proposal was being studied following complaints from the public and members of parliament about internet connectivity problems in locations without residential settlements but which serve as major transportation routes or economic activity centres.

He said the existing approach, which is based on coverage in populated areas, should be reconsidered by taking into account the concept of Coverage of Economic Areas to ensure that connectivity needs in economic areas were also given due attention.

"We want to propose at the ITU level whether it would be appropriate to reconsider the standard from COPA to Coverage of Economic Areas. We want to look beyond whether people live in a particular area and consider whether economic activities are being carried out there," he said in an interview ahead of the 2026 ITU Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26) today.
Fahmi said areas that warranted attention included major roads, railway lines, ports, coastal areas used by fishermen, as well as tourism and recreational destinations.
He said these areas might not have permanent residents but still required good Internet access to support economic activities and the movement of people.

"Many have complained about Internet connectivity or their network coverage along major routes, roads and places that do not have residents but serve as links between two locations or host economic activities," he said.

Fahmi said recreational areas such as Taman Negara and the islands in Sabah were also among the locations that warranted consideration in Internet coverage planning, as they supported economic activities despite not necessarily being residential areas.
He said the proposal had the potential to broaden the approach to assessing digital connectivity needs, particularly in areas that played an important role in economic activities.
"We see a lot of need to take forward ideas such as this, which have not been discussed so far. So, Malaysia could perhaps be among the first to bring this matter to the ITU level," he said.
Fahmi is in Doha from Nov 6 to 11 to lead the Malaysian delegation to ITU PP-26, with the mission of retaining the country's seat on the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term.

Malaysia's participation in the ITU's highest-level conference, held every four years, also aims to ensure that the country's voice and interests continue to be represented in discussions on the global direction of telecommunications and information and communications technology development.

The move reflects the country's aspiration to remain actively involved in international strategic discussions, not merely keeping abreast of global technological developments but also contributing to shaping their direction.

Malaysia's position on the council also provides an opportunity for the country to share its experience and approaches in addressing connectivity challenges, particularly in telecommunications infrastructure development.
Apart from strengthening diplomatic ties, the membership would also enhance Malaysia's international visibility and reinforce its role in digital cooperation, particularly in the Asia-Pacific region.

The ITU is a specialised agency of the United Nations (UN) responsible for ICT matters, including standardisation, radio spectrum allocation and coordination of global telephone and satellite connections, as well as efforts to bridge the digital divide, worldwide.
303c459194e30387: MELAKA, Nov 7 — Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) track record as a key component of the federal government should serve as a yardstick for Melaka voters to assess the coalition’s capabilities ahead of the 16th Melaka State Election on November 14, said Pasir Gudang Member of Parliament Hassan Abdul Karim.
He said the government led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had a good record in governance, particularly in creating employment opportunities for the people.

“Official government employment and investment statistics show that hundreds of thousands of new jobs have been and are being generated by the Madani government,” he said in an open message to Melaka voters and the public yesterday.

Citing data from the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), Hassan said the domestic economy had generated an average of 20,000 to 35,000 new jobs every quarter between 2023 and 2026, in line with a decline in the unemployment rate to between 3.1 and 3.3 per cent.
He said the RM329.5 billion in approved investments in 2023 were expected to generate more than 127,000 new jobs, including over 36,500 in the digital and technology sectors.

“For 2024 and 2025, approved investments contributed to the creation of between 120,000 and 140,000 new job opportunities across the manufacturing and services sectors,” he said, citing the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA).
Hassan said the government was targeting at least 30,000 new high-skilled and technology-based jobs for local youths and graduates.

He said the government also aimed to create tens of thousands of new medium- and high-income jobs by 2027 through initiatives involving HRD Corp, the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).

Hassan also highlighted foreign investors’ confidence in the national economy, citing Google’s announcement of a US$15 billion (about RM61.1 billion) investment in Malaysia, which is expected to create 37,000 jobs by 2027.

“These are not political propaganda. These are facts that the people of Melaka and Malaysia can assess for themselves as the results of the work of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Madani government in creating jobs for Malaysians,” he said.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting scheduled for November 10. — Bernama

b2c1f4ee456487a3: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah last night graced the official launch of Yayasan Sultan Selangor at a Royal Charity Gala Dinner held in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee celebrations of his reign.

Also present was the Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, accompanied by the Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah and his wife Datin Paduka Seri Afzaa Fadini Datuk Abdul Aziz.
Upon arrival, their Royal Highnesses toured a special exhibition, which featured a retrospective display highlighting Sultan Sharafuddin’s 25-year reign.

In his royal address, Tengku Amir Shah, who chaired the Royal Charity Gala Dinner, said the foundation was a meaningful gift to commemorate his father’s Silver Jubilee, with the aim of creating a lasting impact for generations to come.
“Twenty-five years on the throne is more than a milestone. It is a quarter of a century of service, guidance, and unwavering care for the people of Selangor.
“It is fitting that we mark it not with celebration alone, but with a gift, that will keep giving for generations to come,” he said.
Tengku Amir Shah said Yayasan Sultan Selangor stands on four pillars namely community welfare, education and scholarships, heritage and cultural preservation, as well as emergency assistance.
He said the yayasan would work closely with Yayasan Raja Muda Selangor and Selangor Youth Community to create opportunities, nurture young people and support the welfare of the community.
On the foundation’s education initiative, Tengku Amir Shah said its first Sultan of Selangor Scholar, Atiqah Nor Azlan, began her Master’s in Public Policy at the, University of Oxford, in September.
He expressed hope that many more deserving young Malaysians would benefit from the foundation’s support to study at leading institutions worldwide.

Part of the funds raised at the gala dinner would also be channelled to charitable organisations that had maintained close ties with Sultan Sharafuddin and the Selangor royal family over the past 25 years, he added.
The event also featured a special documentary titled “25 Years – One Enduring Bond”, produced by Bernama TV Creative Video Unit, highlighting key milestones of the Sultan’s 25-year reign. — Bernama
a9ee0f50ac5922f2: ALOR GAJAH: Ketua Menteri Melaka Ab Rauf Yusoh menyifatkan dakwaan berhubung projek pembangunan tidak siap di negeri itu sebagai 'peluru sesat' yang dibangkitkan dalam kempen PRN Melaka.

Pengerusi Barisan Nasional (BN) Melaka itu berkata, dakwaan lebih 50 projek pembangunan masih bermasalah tidak menggambarkan perkembangan terkini kerana sebahagian besar projek telah diselesaikan kerajaan negeri.
"Dalam kempen pilihan raya ini, banyak beri peluru-peluru sesat ini.
"Kalau tengok 2025 memang ada 51 tetapi perjalanan itu telah kita uruskan," katanya dalam temu bual FMT.
Baru-baru ini, Timbalan Setiausaha Agung PKR, G Sivamalar, menggesa Rauf menjelaskan status 55 projek pembangunan yang didakwa masih bermasalah di Melaka.

Mengulas lanjut, Rauf berkata berdasarkan maklumat Unit Perancang Ekonomi Negeri (Upen), sebanyak 571 daripada keseluruhan 588 projek membabitkan kerajaan negeri dan persekutuan disiapkan, bersamaan kira-kira 97%.
Tegasnya, tidak tepat untuk menganggap semua 51 projek yang direkodkan pada 2025 sebagai terbengkalai atau masih belum bermula.
Menurutnya, beberapa projek bermasalah turut diwarisi daripada pentadbiran terdahulu dan menjadi antara perkara diberi perhatian sejak beliau mengambil alih pentadbiran negeri pada Mac 2023.
Tegasnya, tidak tepat untuk menganggap semua 51 projek yang direkodkan pada 2025 sebagai terbengkalai atau masih belum bermula.

Antara projek bermasalah berjaya diselesaikan ialah Planetarium Melaka menerusi kerjasama dengan Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) yang akan akan digunakan sebagai kampus kecerdasan buatan (AI) pertama di negeri berkenaan.
Projek Arab City tak guna duit kerajaan

Mengulas dakwaan Pengerusi Pakatan Harapan (PH) Melaka, Adly Zahari, berkait projek Arab City di Pulau Melaka yang terbengkalai sejak lebih sedekad, Rauf berkata tiada dana kerajaan digunakan sebaliknya menggunakan modal syarikat swasta.
"Saya mahu membetulkan fakta pembangunan itu tidak menggunakan dana kerajaan. Syarikat berkenaan membeli tanah tersebut dan memajukan berdasarkan keupayaan mereka sendiri," katanya.
Bagaimanapun, katanya, kerajaan negeri tetap memantau keadaan kawasan berkenaan bagi memastikan ia tidak terus terbiar tanpa pembangunan.
Isnin lalu, Adly membangkitkan projek Arab City sebagai antara pembangunan lama yang memerlukan penjelasan mengenai kedudukan aset dan hala tuju pemulihannya.

Dilaporkan Sinar Harian, bekas ketua menteri itu menggesa kerajaan negeri mendedahkan secara telus status projek terbengkalai terbabit termasuk jumlah perbelanjaan, pihak bertanggungjawab dan perancangan pemulihan.
Arab City mula dibangunkan pada 2009 ketika pentadbiran BN dengan nilai pembangunan keseluruhan dilaporkan kira-kira RM1.2 bilion bagi tiga fasa.
Projek berkonsepkan Asia Barat itu dirancang sebagai pusat perdagangan dan pelancongan, merangkumi bazar, restoran, muzium serta kemudahan komersial lain.
Bagaimanapun, projek yang dijadualkan siap pada 2012 gagal disempurnakan dan terbiar selama lebih sedekad.
0b192448a9a44b0d: PETALING JAYA: The settlement of the RM50 million fine on former prime minister Najib Razak, ensuring that he could finish the remainder of his jail sentence under house arrest, is likely to boost the morale of Barisan Nasional members, especially with the Melaka polls just a week away, according to an analyst.
Azmi Hassan of Akademi Nusantara said the Umno grassroots would be appreciative of the party leadership's efforts to enable Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
The party's fund raising efforts via a solidarity fund was launched on Sept 18 after Najib was granted a conditional pardon.
"I think Umno grassroots, not only in Melaka but nationally, are happy that the party worked on this. It is a huge boost for BN and Umno in Melaka," he said.

The development is seen by analyst Ahmad Zaharuddin Sani Ahmad Sabri of Global Asia Consulting as a "blessing in disguise" for the party following the confidence and supply agreement signed between the government coalition and the opposition party Bersatu.
Umno's efforts to help Najib could even motivate the party and BN to survive independently, without depending on other coalitions, Zaharuddin said.

"While the agreement may weaken BN's bargaining power in Putrajaya, it could awaken something far more important at the grassroots level, that is, the instinct for political survival (on its own)," he said.
Umno settled the RM50 million fine imposed on Najib on Friday, clearing the way for him to serve the remainder of a jail sentence under house arrest.
However, the Attorney-General’s Chambers has called for the house arrest to be deferred until a review is conducted of the conditional pardon and the High Court order of discharge.
Trouble for Pakatan Harapan in Melaka

Zaharuddin said Pakatan Harapan (PH) would be in a dilemma as it faces a potentially demoralised voter base in Melaka, especially if Najib is placed under house arrest while the coalition leads the unity government.
He said PH had made many compromises on its reform pledges to secure enough parliamentary support to stay in power, especially when it started working with former arch-nemesis BN.

"The greatest danger for PH may not be that of voters suddenly switching to BN or PN. It could be something much quieter but equally devastating — political fatigue, declining enthusiasm and supporters choosing to stay home.
"An angry voter may still be persuaded, but an indifferent voter is far more difficult to mobilise," he said.
According to Zaharuddin, such feelings are particularly relevant among younger and urban voters who once regarded PH as the vehicle for political reforms.
However, he also cautioned against assuming Melaka PH supporters will automatically punish the coalition on the ballot come Nov 14.
"It very much depends on whether Anwar can demonstrate that the (house arrest) arrangement accelerates institutional reforms and improves governance," he added.
A weapon for Bersama?
Azmi said Bersama could use the issue to attack DAP secretary-general Loke Siew Fook, who had promised to resign as transport minister when the house arrest takes place.

Zaharuddin agreed, saying that Bersama could argue to PH supporters that the coalition has become so obsessed with consolidating power in Putrajaya that it is increasingly willing to sacrifice its political principles.
"Bersama's greatest opportunity is not simply to convince voters that PH has failed. It is to persuade politically disillusioned voters that they have another credible choice," he added.
a305600a45a89447: IF you aspire to become a world-class footballer, do what Cristiano Ronaldo did.
He is arguably the greatest player a young footballer can emulate.
Forget about trying to be Lionel Messi.
The Argentinian is probably from another planet, dressed in a Homo sapiens suit.
His style, vision and dribbling are almost impossible to replicate.
And then there was the late Diego Maradona, whom many regard as the greatest player ever to grace the game.
Ronaldo came close to Messi, but the Portuguese, hard as it is to admit, was always one rung below the Argentinian.
It was a sad Thursday when Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football after 23 years wearing Portugal's No. 7 shirt.
In fact, he should have called time on his international career several years ago.
Frankly, the 41-year-old overstayed his welcome.
In recent years, he has become a laughing stock on social media as his pace and ability to take on defenders have declined.
Yet his timing remains exceptional, and he is still among the Saudi Pro League's leading goalscorers with Al-Nassr.
CR7 loves football.
His discipline and dedication are qualities few can emulate.
However, age catches up with every footballer, and sadly, Ronaldo is no longer the player he once was.
He has scored some unbelievable goals, earning his place among the greatest forwards ever to grace the game.
One of his best was the bicycle kick against Juventus in the 2018 Champions League quarter-final for Real Madrid.

And who could forget his remarkable goal for Juventus against Sampdoria in Serie A in 2019? Ronaldo jumped 71cm off the ground, reaching a peak height of 2.56 metres, well above the crossbar, to score with a stunning header.
However, he should have retired from international football after the 2022 World Cup.
One could argue that he continued in the hope of winning the World Cup, a dream that remained unfulfilled at this year's tournament.
It will probably be Ronaldo's greatest regret.
He has won almost everything football has to offer, except the biggest prize.
Selfish, some may call him, but he loved his country and wore the Portuguese badge with pride in every match.
That was his motivation and driving force, as he rarely declined a call-up. Unlike some players who pick and choose when to turn out for their country.
One wonders how much longer he can continue as he chases the milestone of becoming the first player to score 1,000 career goals.
He has scored 985 and needs just 15 more to reach that remarkable target.
It is sad to see so many people making fun of Ronaldo on social media, mocking his declining pace and dribbling ability in matches for Al-Nassr.
But age catches up with every footballer, and Ronaldo deserves credit for continuing to compete against players much younger than him.
His declining physical ability does not diminish what aspiring footballers can learn from his discipline, dedication and approach to fitness.
In today's game, almost every youngster wants to emulate Messi and feels proud to be compared to the Argentinian.
But forget about trying to replicate Messi. The closest you can get is touching his feet, especially for aspiring footballers in Malaysia.
Ronaldo, on the other hand, is the perfect role model.
If young players can train as hard as he does and adopt his approach to fitness, diet and discipline, they will give themselves a better chance of succeeding.
Many players have spoken about his extraordinary work ethic.
Even after training, he heads to the gym, swims and jogs to keep himself in peak condition.
Fans will miss his famous "Siuuu" celebration in international football, but one hopes he will return as Portugal's coach and lead the country to glory.
This is a man who simply loves football.
And as a multimillionaire, he has little need to return to the game for financial reasons.
One can only guess that he will eventually find his way back as a coach.
For Malaysian footballers, scoring goals like Ronaldo does not warrant a
"Siuuu" celebration.
It is about sustainability and consistency, which come only through hard work.
Many people have made fun of Ronaldo, including former FIFA president Sepp Blatter, who once labelled him a military-style robot.
Ronaldo played in the same era as Messi. Of course, he needed to be tougher and meaner to compete with the Argentinian.
Ronaldo will go down as the greatest footballer a young player can realistically hope to emulate, not Messi, nor Maradona.
While Messi may be the better footballer, Ronaldo is the example of what dedication, discipline and hard work can achieve.
Adeus, Ronaldo.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
a460ba6ae76fe37c: SHAH ALAM, Nov 7 — The Selangor State Executive Council has directed all local authorities in the state to take immediate enforcement action against unlicensed poultry slaughterhouses.

State Islamic Religious Affairs and Innovation Committee chairman Mohammad Fahmi Ngah said the action would target premises operating without licences from local authorities and those without certified slaughterers.
“Enforcement action must be carried out in accordance with existing laws to ensure that these premises are closed and, where appropriate, demolished.
“This is to prevent non-halal chicken from entering the state’s supply chain, an issue that has raised concerns among Muslims in Selangor,” he said in a statement yesterday.

Mohammad Fahmi also advised the public, particularly Muslims, to purchase raw or cooked chicken only from premises with valid Malaysian Halal Certification (SPHM) issued by the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim).

He said the public could check the list of halal-certified premises through the Halal Malaysia Portal at www.halal.gov.my and report any suspected unlicensed poultry slaughterhouses to the local authorities or the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais).
“The Selangor government remains committed to ensuring a steady supply of halal chicken at affordable prices for the people of the state,” he said. — Bernama
c37c46f45c1f1e41: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Singapore-headquartered Bitdeer Technologies Group (Bitdeer) has expressed its intention to continue investing in Malaysia due to its confidence in the Madani government’s direction and policies on digital transformation.

“The Madani government will continue to facilitate strategic investments such as this to ensure that the growth of the digital economy also strengthens local industries and creates more high-value job opportunities for Malaysians,” Anwar added. — Bernama

c6e7d600c83cd936: SINGAPORE, Nov 7 — A Singaporean man allegedly involved in a Cambodian-based scam syndicate was deported from Vietnam and arrested by the Singapore Police Force (SPF) upon arrival at Changi Airport on Friday (November 6).
Lam Yong Yan, 27, had been detained by Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security for immigration offences since November 19, 2025.
He was deported from the country on Friday after investigations were completed.

Lam is believed to be a member of the crime ring dismantled by the SPF and Cambodian police in September 2025, which orchestrated Government official impersonation scams targeted at fellow Singaporeans.
Police said at least 528 victims collectively lost about S$53 million (RM168 million).
The man will be charged in court on Saturday with facilitating the commission of a serious offence, in furtherance of the illegal purpose of a locally linked organised criminal group.
He faces a jail term of up to five years, a fine of up to S$100,000 (RM317,000), or both, if found guilty.
Lam is among the 36 people sought by local police.
A total of 23 Singaporeans and six Malaysians are still on the run.

Director of the Criminal Investigation Department Senior Assistant Commissioner of Police Julius Lim said on Friday that Singapore deeply appreciates the support and close co-operation of Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security in securing Lam’s return.
“Those who prey on victims in Singapore should know that crossing borders does not put them beyond the reach of the law,” he stated.
“The SPF will work with our international partners to hold them accountable, however far they go.”

Anyone with information on the whereabouts of the remaining suspects should call the SPF hotline at 1800-255-0000, or +65 6255 0000 for overseas callers, or submit information online at www.police.gov.sgi-witness.
All information received will be kept confidential. — AsiaOne
9c92a090b3ea2f50: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Malaysia must accelerate the modernisation of its agricultural sector and improve production efficiency to strengthen food security amid growing challenges, said Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.

He said Malaysia could learn from countries such as Brazil, which had significantly increased its agricultural output, particularly corn, through a market guarantee system rather than relying solely on subsidies.

Recounting his meeting with his Brazilian counterpart, Mohamad said Brazil’s approach did not involve providing subsidies to farmers. Instead, the government guaranteed to purchase produce that could not be sold in the market.

“Regardless of how much they produce, the government guarantees to buy any unsold produce. This motivates farmers to work harder and increase their output, knowing that the government will purchase what they cannot sell,” he said.

He was speaking at the Malaysia Madani Intellectual Forum Series 14 here last night, moderated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Also present were Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir, SD Guthrie Berhad Group President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Mohd Haris Mohd Arshad, and PNB Research Institute CEO Sarena Che Omar.
On the RM2.6 billion in subsidies allocated for local paddy production, Mohamad said calls to discontinue the subsidies and rely solely on government purchases of rice were not appropriate.
He said paddy farmers still needed continued support and encouragement to improve production.

“There has been progress, but we are moving a little slowly. At Mada (Muda Agricultural Development Authority), yields of eight to nine tonnes can already be achieved, although not by many farmers. We need to accelerate the shift towards modernisation,” he said.

On other food commodities, Malaysia had achieved self-sufficiency in fish through the rapid growth of its aquaculture sector, he said, adding that domestic chicken and egg production was also sufficient to meet the country’s needs.
To reduce dependence on imports, the ministry was promoting grain corn cultivation in collaboration with major companies, with a target of meeting 30 per cent of domestic demand by 2030.
The ministry was also expanding onion cultivation based on research by the Malaysian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (Mardi), he said.
Mohamad also stressed the need to strengthen links between agricultural research institutions and universities and farmers, citing Thailand as an example.

“If we visit an agricultural university in Thailand and spend two or three hours there, we can see groups of farmers coming in and out. We need to strengthen this link so that technology developed today can reach rural communities by tomorrow,” he said.

On geopolitical security and future threats, Mohamad urged the public to be prepared for possible cyberwarfare that could disrupt food supply chains, as some European countries were already experiencing supply disruptions and food inflation.
However, he assured that the country’s basic food supplies were sufficient, with rice buffer stocks available for at least six months and fish supplies for eight months.
The Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (Fama) was also prepared to manage physical food distribution should access to digital systems be disrupted, he said.

On weather-related challenges, Mohamad said the ministry was monitoring forecasts by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) on the El Nino phenomenon, which could bring extreme temperatures of up to 40°C after December.
He advised padi farmers to follow the stipulated planting schedules to ensure prudent management of water resources at the three main dams in the Mada area.

“If water levels at the dams become critically low, we will reduce water supply to padi fields and prioritise domestic needs. We take into account the views of scientists, meteorologists and universities to ensure food security is maintained,” he said. — Bernama
f07109cf197633fc: ISTANBUL, Nov 7 — Malaysia views its defence cooperation with Turkiye as a strategic avenue to strengthen its technological capabilities, deepen bilateral relations and contribute to regional stability in South-east Asia.

Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the partnership extends beyond the procurement of defence equipment to include knowledge and technology transfer, while opening up opportunities for broader cooperation in economic, technological, educational and diplomatic fields.
He said military diplomacy was equally important in ensuring South-east Asia remained peaceful and politically stable, particularly amid growing competition and influence from major powers.

“Military diplomacy is also important because we would like to see South-east Asia remain a peaceful region. We have to maintain political stability in Asean as a whole, as we must try to prevent superpowers from exerting influence over Asean member countries,” he said during a session titled “Turkiye From Regional Power to Multi-Regional Actor” at the TRT World Forum 2026 here yesterday.

The session also featured the Director of Foreign Policy Studies at the Foundation for Political, Economic and Social Research (SETA), Prof Murat Yesiltas; Atlantic Council Nonresident Senior Fellow Rich Outzen; American Arab Centre President Farah Al-Atassi; and United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations Jean-Pierre Lacroix.

Ahmad Zahid, who is also the rural and regional development minister, expressed strong confidence that deepened defence and technological cooperation will propel both nations toward realising their ambitious US$10 billion bilateral trade target, while creating a more balanced and vibrant trade relationship.

“From the perspective of both countries, the target is achievable, especially with Malaysia’s procurement of defence and security equipment. We have already received the Littoral Mission Ship (LMS) as well as unmanned aerial vehicles,” he added.
Bilateral trade between Malaysia and Turkiye currently stands at US$5.6 billion, with both countries agreeing in Jan 2026 to raise the figure to US$10 billion within the next five years.
The target reflects their shared commitment to expanding economic ties, with Malaysia among Turkiye’s key trading partners in South-east Asia, alongside Singapore.
Malaysia and Turkiye established formal diplomatic relations on June 17, 1964, and have since maintained close cooperation across various sectors, including politics, trade, economy and education.

The TRT World Forum 2026, themed “A World Without a Centre: Who Leads When the Rules Run Out?”, brings together political leaders, policymakers, academics, media practitioners and civil society representatives from around the world to exchange views on pressing global issues.

Among the prominent Malaysians who have participated in the forum over the years are Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in 2018 and 2019, former international trade and industry minister Tan Sri Rafidah Aziz (2019) and public health expert Prof Tan Sri Jemilah Mahmood (2020). — Bernama
a30f529d6feaed92: LIVERPOOL, Nov 7 — Thierno Barry extended his red-hot streak with a double as Everton beat Coventry 3-1 to climb into fifth place in the Premier League on Friday.
David Moyes’s side trailed to Yann Gboho’s goal early in the second half at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.
But Barry proved too hot for Coventry to handle, netting twice in the space of just five minutes to turn the game in Everton’s favour.
Moyes said this week that Manchester City star Erling Haaland “should be worried” about Barry replacing him as the Premier League’s most lethal striker.
While that might have been hyperbole, Barry has already reached 10 goals this season, surpassing his total for the entire 2025-26 campaign.

That miserable first season with Everton following his move from Villarreal is quickly becoming a distant memory of the in-form 24-year-old, who has six goals in his last seven appearances in all competitions.
Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall scored in the closing minutes to wrap up Everton’s third successive victory in all competitions.
It was a memorable way for Moyes to celebrate a notable milestone as he equalled Harry Catterick’s record of 592 games as Everton manager.
Catterick won the First Division title and the FA Cup with Everton, but Moyes, in his second spell in charge, is still waiting to end the club’s long trophy drought, which dates back to 1995.
Everton are heading in the right direction on the evidence of the last 10 days.

A pair of wins over Newcastle in the League Cup and Premier League were followed by the mature victory against Coventry — all achieved without Jack Grealish, who has been suspended following a breach of discipline after he reportedly skipped a training session.
Deadly Barry
Coventry boss Frank Lampard was left frustrated with a pair of rejected penalty appeals that could have turned the match in his side’s favour.
Lampard, who managed Everton from January 2022 to January 2023, has now seen 16th-placed Coventry beaten three times in their last four games.

In the first meeting between the sides since 2001, Lampard’s men should have taken the lead when Tatsuhiro Sakamoto threaded a pin-point pass to Jack Rudoni but the midfielder shot straight at Jordan Pickford.
Everton defender James Tarkowski escaped without punishment for pulling Caleb Yirenkyi’s hair, an offence that Coventry believed was worthy of a penalty and a red card.
Coventry were frustrated with VAR for the second time when Vitaliy Mykolenko’s shove on Taiwo Awoniyi failed to yield a penalty immediately after half-time.

They finally took the lead in the 52nd minute as Rudoni’s pass squeezed through Everton’s slack marking towards Gboho, who somehow poked past Pickford from six yards despite being surrounded by three defenders.
But the Ivory Coast midfielder’s first goal since his close-season move from Toulouse was swiftly cancelled out by Barry four minutes later.
Mykolenko swung an in-swinging cross into the Coventry area and Barry was left unmarked to thump his header past Carl Rushworth from close-range.
Everton had the momentum and they went in front after 62 minutes.
Barry’s initial shot was saved but the French striker pounced on the rebound to prod home despite Coventry’s appeals for handball.
Barry turned provider in the 81st minute, clipping a pass through to Dewsbury-Hall, who lashed past Rushworth from a tight angle to cap Everton’s stirring fightback. — AFP
b9e1a6d5fc804057: SHAH ALAM: There will be no Deepavali prayers, family meals or festive gatherings for Selangor winger A. Selvan this year as he juggles club and country commitments.

Instead, the 26-year-old will leave for Kuching with the Red Giants on the eve of Deepavali, play a crucial FA Cup semi-final against Kuching City tomorrow before joining the national team for centralised training the following day.
For Selvan, it means spending the festive period away from his parents, M. Anbualagan and C. Sarasbadi, and his four siblings in Seremban, Negri Sembilan.
"Of course, I will miss my family. This time, there is no celebration," said Selvan, who is the youngest of five siblings.
Deepavali is traditionally a family occasion for Selvan, starting with morning prayers at the temple before returning home to share a meal.
But there will be none of that this year.
He has not had time for festive preparations and did not buy new clothes.
"No shopping at all. No clothes, no nothing," he said.
His family understand why he cannot join them.
"They understand. This is a big game, a semi-final. This is my duty for Selangor," he said.
As the youngest child, Selvan grew up receiving money packets from his working elder siblings.
While the dynamic has changed with adulthood, the festive gathering remains special to him.
"The best... If I asked for a shirt or duit raya, they would give me. My brothers and sisters are all working," he said.
His message to his family this year is simple: "Happy Deepavali. Enjoy your day. I will miss them."
Selvan has little time to dwell on what he is missing, with a crucial week ahead.
Selangor hold a 2-1 lead heading into tomorrow's second leg against Kuching City at State Stadium, with victory taking them into the FA Cup final.
A win would mark another milestone in a season where Selvan scored his first official goal for the club against KL City FC in a 3-0 Klang Valley derby victory on Sept 13.
He joined Selangor after consistent performances for Negri Sembilan in the Super League last season, catching the eye with his pace, work rate, and attacking intent.
Primarily a right winger who can also cover other roles, Selvan knows competition for places is stiff.
"If the coach gives me a chance, I want to prove that I can score, provide an assist or do something for the team," he said.
The fixture carries extra significance for the winger, whose last silverware was the 2021 Premier League title with Negri.
He believes Selangor can finish the season with a trophy.
"I am confident. This year we can win a trophy," he said.
A day after the match, Selvan will join the national team for friendlies against China on Nov 14 and Yemen three days later.
The call-up ends a long wait after being on the standby list under former national coach Kim Pan Gon since 2022.

"Before I came here, the coach told me I would definitely get a national team chance. He said if I came here, played and got opportunities, I would get the chance. He was 100 per cent sure," said Selvan.
Despite missing the celebrations, he has no regrets.
"I'm happy to get the national team call-up. I've waited a long time for this opportunity," he added.

9ef6bf25e2481ca9: ISTANBUL, Nov 7 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi paid a courtesy call on Turkiye President Recep Tayyip Erdogan here on Friday, with discussions focusing on strengthening bilateral relations and increasing Malaysia-Turkiye trade value.

The 30-minute meeting, starting at 4pm local time (9pm Malaysian time), occurred shortly after Erdogan launched the TRT World Forum 2026 at the Istanbul Congress Centre (ICC), before Ahmad Zahid joined a session titled “Turkiye From Regional Power to Multi-Regional Actor”.

During the meeting, both countries agreed to increase their bilateral trade target from US$5.6 billion in 2025 to US$10 billion by 2030, following the establishment of the High-Level Strategic Cooperation Council (HLSCC), which held its inaugural meeting in Ankara last January.

Ahmad Zahid also touched on Turkiye’s role as the 12th Asean Sectoral Dialogue Partner and Malaysia’s commitment as the coordinating country for Asean-Turkiye relations to expand strategic cooperation between both parties.

He also expressed appreciation for Turkiye’s firm commitment to championing regional peace, including its active involvement in Syria, Lebanon and Palestine, alongside its role as a mediator in the Russia-Ukraine conflict through the “Istanbul Process”.

Discussions also covered developments in diplomatic efforts to ease tensions between the United States and Iran, including joint initiatives mobilised by Turkiye alongside Pakistan, Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

Furthermore, Ahmad Zahid conveyed Malaysia’s strong support for Turkiye’s role in hosting the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), scheduled to take place in Antalya on November 11 and 12.

Earlier, Ahmad Zahid received a courtesy call from Turkiye’s Council of Higher Education (YOK) President Prof Erol Ozvar at the hotel where he is staying here, besides holding a bilateral meeting with Turkiye Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz at the ICC.

88bc0a283070a360: NEW YORK, Nov 7 — Faculty members at Cornell University on Friday passed a no-confidence resolution against the elite college’s leadership over its handling of an alleged gang rape that has sparked outcry in the United States.
The vote is not binding but marks a strong symbolic rebuke of administrators at Ivy League college in New York state.

According to a lawsuit, a female student was assaulted by seven male students at a fraternity house on campus. Following her initial allegations in 2024, Cornell shut down the fraternity – a male social club – and temporarily suspended the accused students, two of whom were later expelled.
But critics say the college was too lenient, and protests in several US cities last month demanded accountability.
Friday’s resolution states that the faculty “has no confidence in the ability of the central administration to effectively address the ongoing crisis of sexual assault at Cornell University.”
It passed by a vote of 75-50, with five abstentions.
The alleged gang rape has piled scrutiny on Cornell, which has commissioned an independent probe into its handling of the case.
Cornell’s president in October suspended fraternity parties on campus for the remaining academic year as part of several preliminary measures aiming to address sexual assault.
Meanwhile, New York state prosecutors have reopened a criminal investigation into the incident after local authorities said they declined to pursue the case in 2024 over an apparent lack of evidence.
Cornell’s Board of Trustees, which is the college’s top governing body, on Friday voiced support for university President Laurence Kotlikoff.

“Today’s Faculty Senate vote reflects the deep anger across our campus and sends a clear signal that what happened to Jane Doe is unacceptable,” Board Chair Anne Smalling said in a statement, referring to the female student who brought the gang rape allegation.

“The Board of Trustees remains confident that President Kotlikoff and his administration are the right leaders to thoughtfully and comprehensively address the serious problem of sexual assault on our campus.” — AFP

1dcf092e56494df2: DUCATI's Marc Marquez could clinch a record-equalling eighth MotoGP title in Qatar this weekend, but the reigning champion would rather not be there amid paddock unease over racing so close to a regional conflict.
MotoGP officials told teams in Malaysia on Sunday they had received no information warranting a change to the Qatar Grand Prix, despite riders' concerns about the war against Iran.

The race at the Lusail International Circuit, originally scheduled for April, was postponed to November 6 to 8 due to the conflict, with seven-times champion Marquez among those seeking further assurances.

"Not the best place to be but, in the end, we have a contract and we are ready to race here in Qatar," said Marquez, who can equal Giacomo Agostini's haul of eight world championships in the premier class.
"I tried to arrive as late as possible and I will leave as soon as possible... You can see that some people are affected a bit more, some people a bit less.
"But in the end, we must be professional."
Marquez's remark contrasted with the stance taken by Aprilia, who have been vocal about wanting to race in Qatar as they look to salvage a campaign that seemed theirs to win months ago.
MotoGP has said independent risk assessments show it is safe to race, while Qatar has given official assurances and guarantees that teams and riders will not be stranded if the conflict escalates.
APRILIA DISMISS SAFETY DEBATE
"If the organisers say it's safe, we have to go. There's not much to debate. Honestly, I don't understand all this fuss that's being made," Aprilia boss Massimo Rivola told AS.
"I want to go. If you don't want to do this job, you stay home."
But those assurances did not stop Yamaha from withdrawing after the Japanese manufacturer cited "company-wide travel restrictions."
MotoGP said the team could face "sporting consequences" for not honouring its contract, a decision for governing body FIM, which did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.
"I don't want to go. Like everybody," Pramac Racing's Jack Miller had said in Sepang.

"They can attack us at any angle. Both financially and on the sporting side with our licences and also the team... Do I want to hurt the team? Not at all. But at the same time, I don't feel like pushing the horse to race."
Trackhouse rider Raul Fernandez said it had been a "strange weekend" since arriving in Qatar.
"The tension of there being a war going on and you being right in the thick of it... for the people working there, it's not exactly the ideal atmosphere," he said.
MATCH POINT FOR MARQUEZ
Marquez leads with 399 points – 44 ahead of Aprilia's Jorge Martin, who led earlier in the season, and 67 clear of Marco Bezzecchi, once a clear favourite after winning four of the first seven races.
"I'm happy to be heading to Qatar. It's a track I really like," Bezzecchi said.
Martin, who was declared fit on Friday after withdrawing from Malaysia with a fractured wrist, is eager to return after he saw his title hopes slowly fade.

"I went back to Spain to continue the treatment I need to recover from the injury and to get to Qatar in the best shape possible. Now we'll see how the body responds," the 2024 champion said. — REUTERS

291efe144b01be10: PETALING JAYA: Kerajaan digesa menubuhkan sebuah panel bebas bagi menyiasat aduan syarikat terjejas akibat usaha sama bermasalah yang dikaitkan dengan Tabung Haji (TH), selain meneroka saluran untuk mendapatkan tebus rugi.

Ahmad Zaharuddin Sani Ahmad Sabri dari Global Asia Consulting berkata, penelitian tidak patut hanya tertumpu kepada kerugian dialami dana jemaah haji itu, sebaliknya perlu merangkumi layanan terhadap rakan kongsi, pembekal dan pemiutangnya.

"Cadangan saya mudah: wujudkan proses penyerahan bukti secara sulit dengan had masa, lindungi pengadu mempunyai asas kukuh daripada sebarang tindakan balas dan umum dapatan panel tanpa menjejaskan prosiding undang-undang sedang berjalan," katanya kepada FMT.

Beliau mencadangkan sebuah panel ditubuhkan, sebaik-baiknya di bawah pengawasan Parlimen, yang dianggotai pakar dalam bidang perakaunan forensik, undang-undang korporat, insolvensi dan tadbir urus sektor awam.
"Jika institusi awam dipertanggungjawabkan untuk melindungi simpanan rakyat, ia juga perlu bertanggungjawab terhadap cara penggunaan kuasa dalam urusan perniagaan pihak lain."
Zaharuddin berkata, semakan itu perlu membezakan kerugian komersial biasa dengan pertikaian kontrak, kegagalan tadbir urus dan kemungkinan berlaku salah laku jenayah.
"Bukan setiap pelaburan gagal merupakan rasuah, tetapi setiap transaksi meragukan juga tidak patut diketepikan sewenang-wenangnya sebagai keputusan perniagaan."

Gesaan itu susulan pertuduhan terhadap bekas ketua pegawai eksekutif TH, Johan Abdullah dan bekas ketua pegawai kewangan, Rozaida Omar pada 22 Okt lalu atas dakwaan menggunakan penilaian hartanah yang dilambungkan nilainya secara tidak wajar bagi membolehkan pembayaran hibah berjumlah RM3.3 bilion pada 2017.
Kedua-duanya mengaku tidak bersalah.
