9ae969a061b92e34: Kita semua wajar menzahirkan rasa terima kasih yang tidak terhingga kepada Presiden PAS Hadi Awang. Selama berdekad rakyat Malaysia yang biasa sering tersilap langkah dalam mengendalikan perbezaan politik dengan menggunakan istilah sekular yang membosankan seperti ‘perbezaan dasar’, ‘percanggahan ekonomi’, atau ‘perdebatan perlembagaan’. Alangkah remehnya semua itu.

Sebagai pelopor kepimpinan agama, jaguh PAS ini secara bersendirian telah mengangkat wacana politik tempatan menjadi sebuah medan pertempuran kosmik yang berunsur kiamat. Penganalisis politik, badan pemerhati bebas, dan ahli politik pembangkang mungkin bimbang melihat bahasanya yang ‘sangat memecahbelahkan, berunsur agama, dan tajam’, namun mereka sebenarnya tidak mempunyai wawasan untuk menghargai keindahan seni di sebalik kepelbagaian kosa kata negatif beliau. Bagi sesiapa yang cuba memahami bagaimana seorang tokoh yang begitu ‘pakar’ dalam Islam memilih untuk menjaga bahasanya di arena politik, berikut adalah panduan mudah untuk memahami ‘kelas induk’ tentang kesopanan yang sedang beliau tunjukkan kepada dunia.
Doktrin dajal

Mengapa perlu berdebat tentang terma-terma perjanjian perundangan yang biasa jika anda boleh memetik penjelmaan kejelekan mutlak yang nyata? Pada November 2026, apabila kerajaan dan pembangkang mengutarakan cadangan Perjanjian Keyakinan dan Perbekalan (CSA) yang bersifat rutin, pemimpin biasa mungkin akan berdebat tentang peruntukan fiskal. Tetapi bukan maestro kita. Hadi dengan pantas mendiagnosis gencatan senjata rentas parti itu sebagai ‘pendekatan dajal di akhir zaman’. Dengan menyamakan kompromi politik dengan Al-Masih ad-Dajjal (Al-Masih Palsu)—tokoh penipuan mutlak dalam eskatologi Islam—beliau mengingatkan kita semua bahawa kerjasama dwiparti bukan sekadar tadbir urus yang buruk, malah ia merupakan petanda awal kepada perang armageddon.
Sosiologi tahap tinggi

Pada tahun 2022, Hadi dengan penuh bergaya telah mempermudah isu jenayah kewangan global yang kompleks dan sistemik. Tatkala agensi pencegahan rasuah membazirkan berjuta-juta ringgit untuk mengkaji kelemahan institusi dan kecacatan sistem perolehan, Hadi berjaya merungkai rahsia tersebut dengan mengisytiharkan golongan bukan Islam dan bukan Bumiputera sebagai ‘punca rasuah’ di Malaysia. Apabila kumpulan masyarakat sivil seperti Transparency International Malaysia (TI-M) membantah keras kerana menyifatkannya sebagai xenofobia dan hasutan, mereka jelas terlepas pandang nuansa teologi ini: mengapa perlu memperbaiki sistem yang rosak jika anda boleh menyalahkan satu kelompok demografi sahaja?
Kelas tatabahasa dari Dewan yang mulia

Kesopanan Parlimen sudah dianggap ketinggalan zaman. Pada tahun 2025, ketika perdebatan Parlimen yang serius sedang berlangsung, Hadi memutuskan untuk memberikan Dewan Rakyat satu pengajaran langsung mengenai kehalusan bahasa kebangsaan. Apabila merujuk kepada sekumpulan kecil orang Barat berkulit putih, beliau melangkau terus kata ganti nama manusia yang standard dan memilih penjodoh bilangan haiwan iaitu ‘ekor’. Walaupun penggubal undang-undang mempersoalkan adab asas beliau, pencinta bahasa harus mengagumi komitmen beliau yang melayan musuh geopolitik seperti haiwan ternakan yang berkeliaran.
Mengendalikan golongan marhaen intelektual

Sikap konsisten adalah momok bagi minda yang sempit. Apabila empat pemimpin Melayu DAP mempunyai keberanian untuk mempersoalkan pendirian ideologi Hadi yang sering berubah-ubah selama ini, beliau tidak membuang masa untuk membacakan dalil suci kepada mereka. Sebaliknya, beliau secara terbuka memperlekehkan mereka sebagai ‘kurang pendidikan’. Ini adalah taktik perdebatan yang sempurna: jika seseorang menunjukkan ketidakkonsistenan anda, ingatkan sahaja mereka bahawa mereka tidak mempunyai ‘PhD kerohanian’ yang diperlukan untuk memahaminya.
Seni persahabatan yang fleksibel: Pakatan yang kerap berubah

Sepanjang beberapa dekad, jaguh PAS ini melayan pakatan politik seperti musim fesyen—sangat mudah dibuang dan bergantung sepenuhnya pada keadaan cuaca. Lihat sahaja hubungan pasang surut beliau selama berdekad dengan DAP.

Semasa tahun-tahun kegemilangan gabungan Barisan Alternatif dan Pakatan Rakyat (1999–2013), Hadi berkongsi pentas dengan pemimpin DAP yang sama, yang beliau bidas hari ini. Ketika itu, kerjasama politik (tahaluf siyasi) dijulang sebagai perjuangan yang mulia dan strategik. DAP bukanlah ancaman eksistensial; mereka adalah rakan kongsi dalam kempen bersejarah untuk menumbangkan kerajaan pemerintah.

Namun, beralih ke Muktamar PAS pada 2015, parti itu secara tiba-tiba memutuskan hubungan dengan DAP tanpa sebarang perdebatan. Dalam sekelip mata, bekas sekutu itu ditukar secara retroaktif menjadi musuh ideologi yang paling ketara. Ahli PAS progresif yang berani mempersoalkan pusingan-U yang mengejut ini telah disingkirkan sepenuhnya daripada kepimpinan, sehingga mereka akhirnya keluar untuk menubuhkan parti serpihan, Amanah.

Fleksibiliti itu tidak berhenti di situ. Menjelang tahun 2019, Hadi menandatangani piagam Muafakat Nasional dengan Umno—musuh ketat yang pernah dikutuk sekeras-kerasnya dalam ‘Amanat Haji Hadi’ yang terkenal pada tahun 1981. Pada tahun 2020, beliau beralih arah lagi untuk menerajui Perikatan Nasional. Ini adalah satu kelas induk dalam teologi mengikut situasi: sesuatu pakatan itu dianggap suci sehinggalah ke saat ia tidak lagi memberi keuntungan politik, dan pada waktu itulah ia akan dipadamkan daripada ingatan sejarah.
Safari politik ahli zoologi amatur

Beralih daripada kata ganti nama Parlimen yang khusus kepada alam liar yang lebih luas, maestro agung kita turut bertindak sebagai pemandu safari politik yang berwawasan. Beliau menghidangkan negara dengan himpunan haiwan yang dinamik dan berunsur kitab, sehingga beliau mendapat gelaran mesra sebagai ‘ahli zoologi amatur’. Walaupun penyokong setianya bertegas bahawa tindakan beliau yang kerap merujuk kepada alam haiwan hanyalah satu latihan tinggi dalam metafora sejarah dan agama yang mendalam, kreativiti bahasa yang ditunjukkan sebenarnya sangat mengagumkan.

Di bawah pemerhatian taksonominya, Umno yang parah pernah didiagnosis sebagai ‘itik patah kaki’ bagi menghalalkan tindakan PAS mengambil alih stereng kepimpinan. Sementara itu, golongan oportunis sekular dan mereka yang menuntut pembaharuan moral gaya Barat diturunkan pangkat dengan pantas sebagai ‘binatang yang tidak berakal’. Jika anda berani mengkritik paradigma beliau yang berubah-ubah, anda akan dimasukkan ke dalam kandang haiwannya sama ada sebagai ‘kera’ yang hiperaktif, ‘anjing’ yang menyalak tanpa henti, atau simbol kebobrokan moral sistemik seperti ‘khinzir’. Malah, acuan pendidikan yang kaya ini telah memberi inspirasi kepada pengikutnya; kerana terlalu ingin meniru naluri tajam sang guru, ahli Parlimen PAS baru-baru ini terbang ke alam burung dengan melabel Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim sebagai ‘burung tiong’ untuk mempersendakannya sebagai ruang gema tanpa minda bagi dasar luar negara.
Ironi bahasa

Ini membawa kita kepada paradoks komedi mutlak dalam politik Malaysia moden: ironi yang mendalam apabila menggunakan kosa kata suci dari langit untuk melakukan aktiviti membaling lumpur (tuduh-menuduh) yang bersifat transaksi harian.

Islam mempunyai tradisi linguistik yang kaya yang direka untuk memberi inspirasi kepada renungan rohani, kebenaran etika, dan rahmat sejagat. Namun, di tangan kepimpinan PAS, kosa kata ini dijadikan senjata sebagai alat politik yang sangat khusus. Apabila pertikaian dasar yang biasa diperbesar-besarkan secara rekaan menjadi pertempuran kosmik antara cahaya ketuhanan dan kegelapan mutlak, nilai kesucian itu telah diperlekehkan secara sistemik. Kosa kata tentang kebenaran mutlak diturunkan taraf menjadi sekadar kayu pemukul untuk perebutan kuasa di Parlimen.

Pembalikan moral terbesar terletak pada pelaksanaannya. Walaupun agama amat menekankan sifat rendah diri, menahan diri, dan mengelakkan fitnah, retorik politik jenis ini mencapai perkara yang sebaliknya—mengubah tadbir urus rutin menjadi sebuah teater tidak masuk akal yang penuh dengan api dan belerang.

Tatkala badan pemantau seperti Pusat Kewartawanan Bebas (CIJ) taasub menjejaki kosa kata beliau sebagai pemacu utama perpecahan berasaskan identiti dan ucapan kebencian semasa pilihan raya, para pembelanya tetap teguh. Mereka berhujah bahawa nada tanpa kompromi ini adalah pertahanan yang kental demi memelihara agama dan kedaulatan.
Pertembungan politik dan kesolehan

Dan siapa yang boleh menyalahkan mereka? Tiada apa yang lebih menggambarkan ‘agama yang aman dan sejagat’ melainkan tindakan melabel jiran anda sebagai punca rasuah, rakan Parlimen anda sebagai haiwan, dan tadbir urus asas sebagai kerja ‘masihi palsu’. Ini adalah strategi pemasaran yang berani untuk agama, memastikan sesiapa sahaja yang melihat dari luar mendapat gambaran yang jelas dan tidak dapat dilupakan tentang apa yang berlaku apabila politik dan kesolehan bertembung pada kelajuan maksimum.

Akhirnya, strategi ini membuahkan sebuah tontonan yang amat menghiburkan bagi pemerhati. Dengan bertegas bahawa setiap langkah politik yang biasa adalah sama ada satu tindakan atas tuntutan ketuhanan atau plot oleh dajal, arena politik berubah menjadi sebuah teater yang tidak masuk akal—membuktikan bahawa tiada apa yang dapat menyemarakkan perang rebutan kuasa sekular melainkan taburan debu api dan belerang yang tebal.
Penulis ialah pembaca FMT.
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
f5a8cda77435b240: PETALING JAYA: Compact discs are enjoying an unexpected revival among younger buyers. According to market-research firm Luminate, CD sales in the United States rose 16% in the first half of this year to 16.3 million units, with Gen Z and millennials driving much of that growth.

The more surprising finding is that roughly half of younger CD buyers reportedly do not have a device to play them on. For these consumers, the disc itself is increasingly being treated as an affordable collectable, piece of merchandise or physical connection to an artist rather than simply a way to hear an album

K-pop has played a major role in the resurgence. Elaborately packaged albums can come with photo cards, posters, stickers and multiple collectible editions, helping turn a CD release into something closer to a fan package.

Luminate says K-pop accounted for more than half of this year’s rise in US CD sales, helped by major releases from artists including BTS and ATEEZ. Even after removing K-pop from the figures, however, CD sales were still up 6.7%, suggesting the trend extends beyond one fandom.
Price may also help: CDs are generally cheaper than vinyl and easier to store, giving younger fans a relatively accessible way to own a physical version of music they may otherwise stream.

In the UK, department store John Lewis reported that searches for CD players had risen 96% since July. The Guardian also found teenagers and twenty-somethings browsing CD aisles for reasons ranging from affordability to better sound and a desire to spend less time relying on their phones.

The renewed interest is ostensibly part of a wider push back against entirely digital entertainment. People interviewed by The Guardian in October described returning to CDs, DVDs and other physical formats because they wanted more control over what they watched and listened to.
Some disliked having their tastes constantly tracked and shaped by algorithms, while others were frustrated that streaming services could remove favourite titles without warning.

One collector summed up the appeal neatly: “If you can’t hold it, you don’t own it.” Others said physical media encouraged them to listen to whole albums again rather than endlessly skip between playlists.

That thinking is showing up closer to home, too. Earlier this year, FMT Lifestyle reported that many customers at Kuala Lumpur record shop SputnikRekordz were younger people rediscovering vinyl, CDs and cassettes.
Founder Naza Mohammad said physical formats still held a particular appeal for listeners who wanted to sit down and engage more deliberately with music.
None of this means streaming is in trouble - it remains overwhelmingly dominant, accounting for roughly 82% of US recorded-music revenue in the first half of 2026.
What appears to be changing is the role of physical music. Streaming provides convenience, while a CD can offer artwork, packaging, collectability and the satisfaction of owning something tangible.
For a generation accustomed to almost unlimited music living invisibly inside a phone, that might be precisely the point.
d1b263c3c4adc6d3: WASHINGTON: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Britain's Duchess of Sussex, Meghan Markle, was arrested on Friday on a charge of possessing child sexual abuse material, including photographs of himself with naked underage girls, found in rented storage units in California.

FBI Director Kash Patel said the 82-year-old father-in-law of Prince Harry was taken into custody by federal agents in Florida, where, according to the Daily Mail, the elder Markle, who uses a wheelchair, was a nursing home patient.
"Mr. Markle allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions," Patel said in a statement.
In a criminal complaint filed on Thursday in US District Court in Los Angeles, Markle was charged with one count of "possession of child pornography".
If convicted, Markle could face up to 20 years in prison, the Justice Department said.
Markle, a resident of Lakeland, Florida, made his initial court appearance before a US magistrate judge in nearby Tampa.
The judge ordered him released pending trial on condition that he submit to home detention and electronic monitoring, the US Attorney's Office in Los Angeles said in a statement.
No plea was entered, and an arraignment is not expected for several weeks, according to the statement.
Markle's defence counsel was not immediately known, and it was not clear when he might be transferred to California to face the charge against him.

According to an FBI affidavit filed as part of the criminal complaint, Markle kept the sexually explicit material in question in two Los Angeles-area storage units he had rented since 2008. Agents searched the units last week after obtaining a warrant.
Agents seized approximately 78 items, including slides, 35mm film negatives and books containing child sexual abuse images, according to the affidavit.

The 13-page document stated that at least two frames on film negatives showed a man identified by a witness as Markle with a "nude pre-pubescent girl" in poses "designed to elicit a sexual response in the viewer". In one image, the man appeared to be fondling the girl's genitalia.
Buckingham Palace and a spokesperson for Meghan Markle did not respond to requests for comment.
Authorities in the Philippines, where Thomas Markle had previously lived for some time, began investigating him last month over allegations that he possessed child sexual abuse images.

British police last month said they would refer allegations against him to overseas law enforcement agencies after finding that the claims had not been passed to other authorities when they were first received.

The FBI began its investigation into Markle in October, according to its affidavit, after hearing from a witness who said they had discovered suspected child abuse material among Markle's possessions in the Philippines.
The FBI also spoke last month with a second witness, who was also unidentified in the affidavit, and who said Markle rented at least one storage unit in California.
At least one of the photographs reviewed by the FBI showed that Markle was staying at a hotel or motel in the Philippines, based on the logo seen on the pillows on the bed.
Markle denied the accusations of possessing child sexual abuse material when they initially came to light, telling the Daily Mail they were untrue and "sick lies".
Meghan Markle, an American actor who married King Charles' younger son in 2018, has said she was "deeply distressed" by the allegations.

85f7c48027d76873: LOS ANGELES: American rapper Macklemore, an outspoken critic of Israel's war in Gaza, said on Friday that major US concert venues including New York's Madison Square Garden refused to book his Free Palestine tour that just concluded three dates in Europe.

The "Thrift Shop" performer launched the effort after he was removed as the opening act on musician Ed Sheeran's concert tour in August. Macklemore said at the time that stadium owners had objected to him saying "Free Palestine" on stage.

Since then, nine US venues declined to allow him to book available dates through the end of the year, Macklemore said on social media. The venues included Madison Square Garden and the Kia Forum in Los Angeles.
"The shows were not going to be allowed to happen in these venues," he said in a post. "In over 20 years of touring, I've never experienced anything like this."

A spokesman for MSG Entertainment, which operates Madison Square Garden and other venues, said its properties are among "the busiest venues in the world with extremely limited availability" and that Macklemore is "not an arena-level act".
Representatives for the Kia Forum did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Macklemore played Free Palestine shows in Dublin, Paris and London to raise funds for organisations that support the Palestinian people. The musician said he would work with other artists and organisers to do more performances for the cause.

"We live in a country that prides itself on freedom of speech," he wrote. "Yet we've reached a point where a handful of billionaires can decide which causes are acceptable, which voices are welcome and which human lives are worth defending."

0b554f50751367c5: ASUNCION: Paraguayan senators on Friday voted to impeach President Santiago Pena over the collapse of a major bank that locked almost half the population out of their accounts and triggered widespread protests.
Pena had offered his resignation over the disaster, but lawmakers pressed ahead with impeachment proceedings that would strip him of the immunity granted to former presidents.
He did not attend the trial in the Senate despite earlier pledging to defend himself.
"The president is declared guilty of poor performance in his duties," Senate President Basilio Nunez declared after a vote of 44 in favour of impeachment, with one absence among the 45 senators.
Around three million people have been unable to access their money since the Central Bank took control of Ueno Bank on Tuesday and froze its accounts over concerns about its solvency.
A Central Bank official told AFP that advance payments to some affected depositors had begun on Thursday afternoon.
The bank's collapse brought thousands of people onto the streets demanding repercussions for US-backed Pena, who until last year had a stake in Grupo Vazquez, which controlled Ueno.
Lawmakers from Pena's own party backed his impeachment.
Pena, 47, apologised during an address to the nation on Thursday.
"It was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me," he said in a video statement.
'Hurt'
Around 250 people gathered outside Congress awaiting the outcome of the trial, one of them waving a sign that read: "Pena in prison."
On Thursday, thousands protested for a third consecutive night in Asuncion and other cities to demand the return of their money.

"Santiago Pena has hurt so many Paraguayans, so many families, business owners and small business people, including my own son, who had savings in Ueno Bank," Cynthia Farina told AFP at a protest in the capital that police dispersed with tear gas and water cannon.
Advance payments to an unspecified number of affected depositors began on Thursday afternoon, Jose Maciel of the Central Bank's Deposit Guarantee Fund told AFP.
The first phase of aid deposits, of up to around US$1,600, will go to clients who do not have loans and have an account at another bank or institution in Paraguay to receive the funds, Maciel said.
The next beneficiaries "will be announced progressively over the course of the payment process", he said.

Ueno began as a small fintech company with a digital-first model that attracted low-income customers, rapidly becoming a major bank that handled state pensions and the accounts of several state entities.
The opposition accuses Pena of a conflict of interest, which he denies.
The attorney general said it was investigating him for "acts related to the supervision and resolution of Ueno Bank S.A. and the placement of public funds in said entity".
The US Embassy in Paraguay expressed "its solidarity with the Paraguayan people" on Friday, without mentioning the president.
'Victims'
Ueno's downfall shocked the South American country, which is generally considered economically and politically stable.

By impeaching him rather than allowing him to resign, lawmakers have prevented Pena from becoming a senator for life and enjoying immunity from prosecution, constitutional experts and lawmakers told AFP.
Vice-President Pedro Alliana is preparing to complete the current mandate until 2028.
The scandal has claimed the heads of Central Bank President Carlos Carvallo and Interior Minister Enrique Riera.
Eight Ueno executives have been arrested.
Prosecutors on Friday raided the offices of technology company ITTI, which is part of Grupo Vazquez, confiscating hard drives, computers and other items.
"We found a large amount of documents that will be useful for the investigation," prosecutor Francisco Cabrera told reporters.
Nearby Argentina felt the impact of the crisis as some 1,000 ITTI employees were suspended for 30 days without pay.
Football also took a hit.
Ueno Bank sponsors several first-division teams as well as the national team.
"We were also victims of this situation," members of the national team said in a statement on X.

8eadcb9cfa090522: BENTONG: For much of the year, the oil palm plantation in Jalan Karak-Manchis is a quiet place, its ageing community going about life far from the bustle of town.
But when Deepavali comes around, the stillness gives way to festive music, brightly lit homes and the crackle of fireworks as children and grandchildren return to celebrate the festival of lights.
For R. Gopal, 55, and his wife, S. Puspa Devi, 49, the celebration is less about the festivities than the joy of having their five children, aged between 21 and 28, under one roof again.
Born and raised on the estate, Gopal has watched the once-thriving plantation community gradually shrink as families retired, moved away and sought new lives elsewhere.
Yet Deepavali remains a cherished occasion, bringing a fleeting return of the warmth and camaraderie that once defined life on the estate.
"When I was young, more than 150 Indian families were living in the estate. Imagine how much fun we had. Now, only about 20 families remain, as many have retired and moved away.

"My wife and I eagerly look forward to Deepavali because that is when my eldest son, who works in Singapore, and his siblings return home. They usually spend about a week here before heading back to work," he told the New Straits Times.
The grandfather of five said most of the younger generation had left the plantation, many finding work outside Pahang.
These days, their homecomings are largely confined to Deepavali, the estate temple's annual festival or the funeral of a close family member.
For Gopal, the estate only truly comes alive when the children return, filling the neighbourhood with laughter and renewing friendships forged during their younger days.

"For older people like me, what matters most is spending the festive holidays with our children. They are the ones who bring the neighbourhood to life by decorating their homes, setting off firecrackers and playing festive music.
"On Deepavali morning, the entire estate community gathers at the temple within the plantation for prayers. Families dress in matching traditional outfits and greet one another.
"In the past, people would stay up until the early hours preparing special dishes, but these days, many prefer to have food catered," he said.
But beneath the festive cheer lies the quiet realisation that Gopal's own days on the estate are numbered.
With retirement just five years away, he knows that the Deepavali celebrations he has treasured since childhood may soon become memories of a place he once called home.
Like many of his former neighbours, he plans to leave the plantation after retirement, closing another chapter in a community that has steadily grown smaller over the decades.

"After retiring, many of my friends left the estate to live with their children. When I retire, my wife and I plan to move to Johor to stay with our son, but we will make an effort to return for the temple festival.

"Growing up on the estate is something I will always cherish. I often share stories with my grandchildren about my early days working here — living in the old wooden workers' quarters and how all my siblings would help my mother prepare muruku during Deepavali," he said.

9ce835fe79b25d63: LONDON: Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi said he was hungry to fulfil chief executive Vinai Venkatesham's bold claim that the club's long-term goal was to win the Premier League.
When Venkatesham laid out the title target in an interview this week, the claim sparked derision from rival fans.
The north Londoners have not won the English title since 1961 and narrowly avoided relegation on the final day of last season.
Tottenham, who have finished 17th for the last two seasons, are currently ninth in the top-flight table after recovering from a dismal start.
They trail leaders Arsenal by 12 points ahead of Saturday's trip to Leeds.
But asked about Venkatesham's optimistic remark, De Zerbi told reporters he was encouraged by his belief in the potential for success.
"It was great to hear what Vinai said. I think the first thing for the people to stay in this club, to work in this club is to be ambitious, but to be ambitious you have to show," he said.
"And you have to show the right mentality every day, game by game because just with the words is not enough.
"What Vinai, the Lewis family, Johan Lange, what they are doing is something special because in the last two seasons, I think you can see they are changing a lot of things in this club.
"And for me as a coach, for my staff, for the players, we have to show to the best self to stay in this club."
A transfer window of lavish spending on Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and a host of other new recruits raised hopes of a successful season for Tottenham.
However, De Zerbi's team failed to win any of their first six league games.
They turned the tide with a draw at Manchester United before wins over Coventry, Chelsea and Crystal Palace lifted them away from the relegation zone.
"With the right behaviour, with the right mentality, to be hungry every day and to make a result. This is the best thing to do from our side," De Zerbi said of the secret to Tottenham's revival.
012ae01d66eaf598: WASHINGTON: US secretary of state Marco Rubio will head to France next week for a gathering of G7 foreign ministers, the state department said Friday, as pressure mounts over wars in the Middle East and Ukraine.
This marks Rubio's first trip abroad since the Republican Party's sweeping losses in US midterm elections, dealing a sharp blow to President Donald Trump as Democrats won full control of Congress.

While the election's impact on US foreign policy remains to be seen, the G7 meeting on Monday and Tuesday will offer Washington's allies an early opportunity to gauge the Trump administration's thinking.
The US top diplomat's travel to Paris from November 8-10 will see him "advance American interests in engagements with his G7 counterparts," said the state department in a brief statement.

The talks among the Group of Seven advanced economies -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- were originally meant to be held in Marseille. But they were moved to the capital at the last minute.

France's foreign ministry said this was due to logistical reasons, although the shift comes amid weeks of nationwide cost-of-living protests -- developments that have been viewed with concern in the US.

During their two-day gathering, G7 foreign ministers are set to discuss support for Ukraine as it battles Moscow's invasion, alongside efforts to stabilise the Middle East, which has been engulfed in war since US-Israel strikes targeting Iran in February.
The meeting also comes as Russia-Ukraine negotiations, under US mediation, have been scheduled for November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi.
On Thursday, Trump predicted an imminent deal with Russia covering Ukraine and "all of Europe."

Jared Kushner, the president's envoy and son-in-law, said in an X post Thursday that Trump has advanced talks with European leaders "about the need for a broader European security architecture that can help establish the conditions for lasting peace."
Washington's European allies, however, have long rejected Moscow's desire to rewrite the European security architecture.
Next week's foreign ministers meeting brings together officials from the G7 and partner countries including Saudi Arabia, Egypt, South Korea, Brazil and Ukraine.
France's G7 presidency concludes at year-end, with Washington set to next take over the reins.
Rubio's trip also comes amid speculation about his political future. He is widely viewed as a potential successor to Trump in the 2028 US presidential election.
But Rubio has dismissed reports that he was planning to leave, telling The New York Times on Thursday that it has "always been my plan" to work for Trump until the end of his term.
bead155b855254cd: MELAKA: Bersatu has not issued any official directive to its grassroots to reciprocate support for Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidates in the Melaka election.
Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the party nonetheless welcomed support from any party or voter intending to back its candidates.
"We welcome anyone who believes it is good to support Bersatu. We certainly appreciate it because we want our candidates to win.
"However, we have not issued any directives. Even so, Bersatu members understand what needs to be done," he said after a walkabout with residents at the Sungai Udang constituency hall.
Muhyiddin was responding to reports on PH's readiness to assist the Bersatu machinery.
Earlier, Bersatu deputy president Datuk Seri Ahmad Faizal Azumu also confirmed no official directive was received by the party to do so.
Muhiyiddin then expressed appreciation for any open endorsement from supporters of other parties aimed at ensuring victory for Bersatu candidates.
He also confirmed there was no official cooperation between Bersatu and PH.
He said that early talks were held between party leaders to avoid seat overlaps.
Muhyiddin added that Bersatu remained open to working together with PH.
"Yes, we welcome it. We will not say we want to reject it," he said.
0a48b55afc5b616f: PETALING JAYA: The Industrial Court has dismissed a former human resources manager’s claim of unfair dismissal against technology consulting firm VDart Malaysia Sdn Bhd, ruling that her employment ended when her fixed-term contract expired.

Industrial Court chairman Augustine Anthony said D Elizebeth had failed to establish that the company promised to make her a permanent employee, or that she was dismissed without just cause or excuse.
Elizebeth joined VDart in September 2023 as its human resources and administration manager on a one-year contract, earning RM7,300 a month. Her salary was increased to RM7,500 upon confirmation.

As the contract neared its expiry in September 2024, she sought clarification about her future with the company. VDart subsequently offered her a three-month extension until Dec 13, 2024, which she accepted and signed.
The company declined to renew her contract when the extension expired.
Elizebeth claimed she had been assured of permanent employment and that the company had asked her to prepare a letter of appointment reflecting her new status.
She argued that the fixed-term arrangement was merely a disguise for permanent employment and sought reinstatement, back wages and other benefits.
However, Anthony found that the documentary evidence did not support her claim that permanent employment had been promised.
He noted that her emails acknowledged the expiry of the original one-year contract and the subsequent three-month extension.
She had also accepted the extension despite the company rejecting her request for a salary increase.
“The claimant’s testimony that she had a legitimate expectation to be employed as a permanent employee is without any merit,” he said in his 28-page award.
Anthony said VDart’s status as a start-up and its project-based operations also supported its decision to employ her on a fixed-term basis.
He concluded that the contracts were fixed-term arrangements and that the final extension had ended naturally through the passage of time.
“The claimant’s contracts of employment for a specific duration of time were genuine fixed-term contracts of employment,” he ruled.
As there had been no dismissal, the question of whether it was without just cause or excuse did not arise. The claim was therefore dismissed.
Dashprit Kaur appeared for Elizebeth while Timothy Dass represented the company.
7aa7ffad250dea19: PPETALING JAYA: Mahkamah Perusahaan menolak tuntutan seorang bekas pengurus sumber manusia terhadap firma perunding teknologi VDart Malaysia Sdn Bhd atas dakwaan pemecatan tidak adil, dengan memutuskan bahawa perkhidmatannya tamat apabila tempoh tetap kontraknya berakhir.

Pengerusi Mahkamah Perusahaan Augustine Anthony berkata D Elizebeth gagal membuktikan bahawa syarikat itu berjanji untuk menjadikannya pekerja tetap atau beliau dipecat tanpa sebab atau alasan yang adil.

Elizebeth menyertai VDart pada September 2023 sebagai pengurus sumber manusia dan pentadbiran dengan kontrak selama setahun, menerima gaji RM7,300 sebulan. Gajinya dinaikkan kepada RM7,500 selepas pengesahan jawatan.

Ketika kontraknya hampir tamat pada September 2024, beliau meminta penjelasan mengenai masa depannya dengan syarikat itu. VDart kemudiannya menawarkan lanjutan kontrak selama tiga bulan sehingga 13 Dis 2024, yang diterima dan ditandatanganinya.
Syarikat itu enggan memperbaharui kontraknya selepas tempoh lanjutan berkenaan tamat.
Elizebeth mendakwa beliau diberi jaminan akan diambil bekerja secara tetap dan syarikat itu memintanya menyediakan surat pelantikan yang mencerminkan status baharunya.

Beliau berhujah bahawa aturan kontrak itu sekadar menyembunyikan hakikat bahawa beliau sebenarnya pekerja tetap, dan menuntut supaya diambil bekerja semula, pembayaran gaji tertungak serta faedah lain.
Bagaimanapun, Anthony mendapati bukti dokumentari tidak menyokong dakwaannya bahawa beliau telah dijanjikan pekerjaan tetap.
Anthony ambil maklum bahawa e-mel Elizebeth mengakui kontrak asal selama setahun telah tamat dan kemudiannya dilanjutkan selama tiga bulan.
Elizebeth juga menerima lanjutan kontrak itu walaupun syarikat berkenaan menolak permintaannya untuk kenaikan gaji.
“Keterangan pihak menuntut bahawa beliau mempunyai jangkaan yang sah untuk diambil bekerja sebagai pekerja tetap langsung tidak berasas,” katanya dalam award setebal 28 halaman.
Anthony berkata status VDart sebagai syarikat pemula dan operasinya yang berasaskan projek turut menyokong keputusannya untuk mengambil Elizebeth bekerja secara kontrak dengan tempoh tetap.
Beliau menyimpulkan bahawa kontrak berkenaan merupakan aturan tempoh tetap dan lanjutan terakhir itu tamat secara semula jadi apabila tempohnya berakhir.
“Kontrak pekerjaan pihak menuntut bagi tempoh tertentu merupakan kontrak pekerjaan tempoh tetap yang tulen,” katanya dalam keputusan itu.
Memandangkan tiada pemecatan berlaku, persoalan sama ada pemecatan itu dilakukan tanpa sebab atau alasan yang adil tidak timbul. Oleh itu, tuntutan berkenaan ditolak.
Dashprit Kaur hadir bagi pihak Elizebeth manakala Timothy Dass mewakili syarikat itu.
d3d920d8cd82072c: PETALING JAYA: Just when we think we have a reasonable understanding of the natural world, scientists uncover something that challenges our assumptions.
Whether it's an animal behaving in an unexpected way or an ecosystem flourishing where none was thought to exist, nature continues to offer plenty of surprises.
Here are five recent global curiosities that demonstrate just how remarkable the world beyond our doorstep can be.
1. Some penguins live in rainforests

Forget icy landscapes and enormous colonies of penguins huddling together against the cold. Deep in New Zealand's coastal rainforests lives the Fiordland crested penguin, or tawaki, a secretive bird with distinctive yellow eyebrows.
Unlike most penguins, tawaki nest in secluded burrows among dense vegetation rather than gathering in large breeding colonies. Their elusive habits have made them exceptionally difficult to study.

Over 12 years, researchers with the Tawaki Project have mapped approximately 1,200 nests across nine fjords, suggesting the population is roughly three times larger than earlier surveys indicated. This reflects improved scientific knowledge, however, rather than a sudden increase in penguin numbers.

Perhaps even more puzzling is their annual journey to feeding grounds before moulting. Despite food being available nearby, the birds undertake extraordinary round trips of 5,000km to 7,000km towards sub-Antarctic waters - for reasons scientists are still investigating.
2. Moths can fool weather radars
In parts of southeastern Australia, weather radars have been displaying what appears to be widespread rainfall - sometimes when not a single drop is falling.
The likely culprits are millions of migrating bogong moths, whose enormous swarms can reflect radar signals much like airborne water droplets.

These insects undertake remarkable seasonal journeys towards the Australian Alps, where they shelter in cool caves and rocky crevices during summer. Their movements have been particularly conspicuous this October, with radar echoes appearing shortly after sunset, when the moths become active.
Australia's Bureau of Meteorology believes the insects account for much of the unusual activity, although other atmospheric conditions can produce similar signals.
Beyond confusing weather watchers, the phenomenon highlights an unexpected application of meteorological technology: radar could help scientists monitor insect movements across vast distances.
3. Ancient forests have become underwater reefs
Off Mozambique's coast, researchers have discovered a remarkable transformation beneath the waves: ancient terrestrial forests that have become thriving marine habitats.
In the shallow waters of the Bazaruto Archipelago, remnants of coastal peatlands submerged by rising seas have formed underwater structures known as peat reefs.
Radiocarbon dating suggests the material originated between approximately 300 and 5,000 years ago, when these landscapes supported vegetation rather than marine life.
Today, the formations provide shelter and feeding opportunities for fish and invertebrates, supporting biodiversity comparable in richness to neighbouring coral reefs.
Unlike conventional reefs, however, these underwater habitats are built upon ancient, carbon-rich terrestrial deposits rather than structures created by living corals.

The discovery raises intriguing questions about how many similar ecosystems remain undocumented along the world's coastlines, and whether these unusual habitats deserve greater conservation attention.
4. Birds are learning songs their ancestors once sang
In a park in Buenos Aires, Argentina, researchers recently heard something they hadn't expected: a bird singing elements of a tune that had disappeared from the area decades earlier.
The song belonged to the rufous-collared sparrow, whose local vocal traditions had been documented during the 1960s.

Using historical records, scientists reconstructed a computer-generated version of the old melody and played it to modern birds.Within three months, a sparrow began imitating parts of the recording, suggesting that elements of a lost vocal tradition could be reintroduced.
The finding has potentially important implications for conservation because many birds learn their songs from others rather than inheriting them entirely through instinct.
When populations decline, those opportunities diminish, potentially affecting communication, territorial behaviour and the ability to attract mates.
Researchers hope such techniques might eventually help threatened species recover important aspects of their vocal behaviour.
5. Scavengers have favourite cuts of meat
Scavengers may have a reputation for eating whatever they can find, but Australian researchers have discovered that some are surprisingly selective diners.
Using camera traps to monitor 40 kangaroo carcasses in New South Wales, scientists examined the feeding preferences of dingoes, wedge-tailed eagles and red foxes.

The results revealed distinct patterns: eagles initially favoured the head and abdomen, while dingoes frequently targeted the tail. Foxes, meanwhile, were often left with whatever the larger, more dominant scavengers hadn't already consumed.
Researchers believe these preferences partly reflect nutritional requirements, particularly the availability of fat-rich tissues.
Interestingly, the animals' choices changed as the carcasses decomposed, with eagles eventually shifting towards more protein-rich portions.
The findings challenge the assumption that scavenging is simply indiscriminate feeding, revealing instead a complex process shaped by nutritional needs, competition and access to food.
4e1637472909334b: PETALING JAYA: There are no laws requiring donations to be audited, says a former auditor who previously served on two of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) oversight panels.
Walter Sandosam said this in reference to a call for authorities to vet funds received by Umno to help former prime minister Najib Razak pay a RM50 million fine.
He said a donation drive launched by the party in September to raise funds for the former prime minister to settle a RM50 million fine was a private and personal initiative.
“No coercion was involved. Umno is not required to divulge details of those who contributed to the initiative,” he told FMT.
Yesterday, DAP’s Tony Pua urged the authorities to audit the donations raised to help settle the fine, which allows Najib to serve the remainder of his corruption sentence under house arrest.
The former Damansara MP said an audit by Bank Negara Malaysia and MACC was vital to ensure the funds raised were legitimate and not laundered.
Sandosam said only donors can call for an audit but pointed out that there was no undertaking at the onset for it to be scrutinised.
“There’s no need for transparency in this case, when even the government can choose what to make public and what not to. Tony is being naughty,” he said.
He also questioned why Pua was talking about the need for these donations to be vetted only after the sum had been collected.
Sandosam said, however, that the entire affair underscored the importance of enacting a political finance bill.
In September, law and institutional reform minister Azalina Othman Said urged all parties to state in writing whether they support or oppose the proposed legislation.
Azalina said the government wanted official responses from all political parties registered with the Registrar of Societies (RoS), which number about 72.
She said the responses would provide evidence of the parties’ positions, rather than relying solely on surveys or other informal feedback.
f8a2cefdf7ad0801: ASUNCION: Paraguayan Senators on Friday voted to impeach President Santiago Pena over the collapse of a major bank that locked almost half the population out of their accounts and triggered widespread protests.
Pena had offered his resignation over the disaster, but lawmakers pressed ahead with impeachment proceedings that would strip him of immunity granted to former presidents.
He did not attend the trial in the Senate despite earlier pledging to defend himself.
The president "is declared guilty of poor performance in his duties," Senate President Basilio Nunez declared after a vote of 44 in favor of impeachment and one absence out of 45 senators.
Around three million people have been unable to access their money since the Central Bank took control of Ueno Bank on Tuesday and froze its accounts over concerns about its solvency.
A Central Bank official told AFP that advance payments to some affected depositors had begun on Thursday afternoon.
The bank's demise brought thousands of people onto the streets demanding repercussions for US-backed Pena, who until last year had a stake in Grupo Vazquez, which controlled Ueno.
Lawmakers from Pena's own party backed his impeachment.
Pena, 47, apologised during an address to the nation on Thursday.
"It was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me," he said in a video statement.
'Hurt'
Around 250 people were gathered outside Congress awaiting the outcome of the trial, one of them waving a sign that read: "Pena in prison."
On Thursday, thousands protested for a third consecutive night in Asuncion and other cities to demand the return of their money.

"Santiago Pena has hurt so many Paraguayans, so many families, business owners and small business people, including my own son, who had savings in Ueno Bank," Cynthia Farina told AFP at a protest in the capital that police dispersed with tear gas and water cannons.
Advance payments to an unspecified number of impacted depositors began on Thursday afternoon, Jose Maciel of the Central Bank's Deposit Guarantee Fund told AFP.
The first phase of aid deposits, up to around US$1,600, will go to clients who don't have loans and have an account at another bank or institution in Paraguay to receive the funds, Maciel said.
The next beneficiaries "will be announced progressively over the course of the payment process," he said.

Ueno began as a small fintech company with a digital-first model that attracted low-income customers, rapidly becoming a major bank that handled state pensions and the accounts of several state entities.
The opposition accuses Pena of a conflict of interest, which he denies.
The Attorney General said it was investigating him for "acts related to the supervision and resolution of Ueno Bank SA and the placement of public funds in said entity."
The US Embassy in Paraguay expressed "its solidarity with the Paraguayan people" on Friday, without mentioning the president.
'Victims'
Ueno's downfall shocked the South American country, which is generally considered economically and politically stable.
By impeaching him rather than letting him resign, lawmakers have prevented Pena from becoming a senator for life and enjoying immunity from prosecution, constitutional experts and lawmakers told AFP.
Vice-president Pedro Alliana is preparing to complete the current mandate until 2028.
The scandal has claimed the heads of Central Bank President Carlos Carvallo and interior minister Enrique Riera.
Eight Ueno executives have been arrested.
Prosecutors on Friday raided the offices of technology company ITTI, which is part of Grupo Vazquez, confiscating hard drives, computers and other items.
"We found a large amount of documents that will be useful for the investigation," prosecutor Francisco Cabrera told reporters.
Nearby Argentina felt the impact of the crisis as some 1,000 ITTI employees were suspended for 30 days without pay.
Football also took a hit.
Ueno Bank sponsors several first division teams as well as the national team.
"We were also victims of this situation," members of the national team said in a statement on X.
ebe4194b3df1a62c: MELAKA: Bersatu's failure to win seats in the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections does not necessarily reflect voter support for the party in Melaka.
Its secretary-general, Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, said the party acknowledged the risks but expected to reduce them through strategic planning and trained machinery.
He said the party's decision to contest seven seats was made after weighing various factors through strategic consideration and careful study.
"After giving it very careful and very thorough consideration, we feel the number that is significant and strategic enough for Bersatu this time is seven seats with the potential for us to win.
"Although we know that in any election there are risks, we have strategic planning and organised and trained machinery.
"So we are confident it can boost the support of the people of Melaka for Bersatu," he said in an interview here.
Bersatu is fielding seven candidates, whereas Wawasan is contesting two seats in Kesidang and Bemban under the PN logo.
Bersatu and Wawasan will also face off in Bemban, which will see a four-cornered fight that includes Parti Bersama Malaysia and an independent.
Azmin said Bersatu was taking a different approach in this election by prioritising wisdom and suitable political strategy.
He said this included fielding candidates in state seats also contested by Pakatan Harapan, even though both sides were seen to have an understanding.
"It may be awkward because we have never been through a situation like this, but as I mentioned earlier, this is the wisdom of the political parties taking part in the Melaka election.
"Although there is cooperation, if they feel there is a winning factor or that victory favours them, then they will field a candidate there.
"But for Bersatu, based on other considerations, for example the candidate is well liked, accepted by voters, has an excellent record and is young, so we feel victory may favour Bersatu," he said.
f33e50a215ecdb78: SANAA: Yemen's Houthis said Saudi airstrikes killed 30 people at a market on Friday, while local authorities accused the Iran-backed group of carrying out the attack.
The Houthis said "several strikes" hit the market in an area under their control in Taiz province, the scene of fierce fighting since the Iran-backed group launched a major offensive in September.
"Saudi enemy aircraft targeted the market in Al-Waziya city with several strikes," the Houthis' health ministry spokesman Anis al-Asbahi said in remarks carried by their Saba news agency.
A health ministry statement said 30 people were killed and eight wounded, adding that rescue teams were searching for bodies under the rubble.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the strikes were fired from a plane that took off from the Saudi base of Khamis Mushait on Friday.
But Yemen's government forces accused the Houthis of firing a ballistic missile at the market, condemning it as a "war crime".
Authorities in Taiz also issued a statement blaming "indiscriminate Houthi missile fire", denying any air raids took place.
Yemen slipped back into war between the Iran-allied Houthis and the Saudi-backed government in July after years of relative calm, opening a new front in the conflict in the Middle East.
Since then, Saudi Arabia has regularly bombed Houthi positions, while the group has multiplied its attacks against the oil-rich kingdom.
Earlier on Friday, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it intercepted a drone in the region of Mecca, Islam's holy city, without specifying where it came from.
The Houthis have claimed responsibility for numerous strikes on Saudi airports, oil facilities and military sites, but they regularly deny targeting the holy cities.
On Thursday, the coalition reported intercepting a Houthi missile around Medina, another sacred city, a claim the group dismissed as "slander".
9b3e93412b83fc28: A man in his 20s showed up to a UK hospital with the hilt of a knife sticking out of his face. The 15 mm blade hidden within went completely through his right eye and through his brain, with the tip of the blade hitting the top of his skull.

Despite the ghastly injury, the man was alive and conscious when he arrived. He could still talk and move all four limbs. His doctors described him as being in a state of agitation. On the Glasgow Coma Scale, he scored a 12 (E3 V4 M5), indicating a "moderate" brain injury, just one point above "mild." He could open his left eye when told, but otherwise kept it closed (E3 score); he could talk and answer questions, but was confused (V4); and he intentionally moved away when pressure was applied to his body (M5).

In a report published Friday in BMJ Case Report, his doctors said they were concerned that in his confused, agitated state he may try to pull the knife out on his own. So, they swiftly sedated and intubated him. They put him on prophylactic treatments for bacterial infections, including tetanus. Then they used images to see what was going on in his head.

23e1a2b46402c7dd: NEW YORK: An allegation of gang rape at the elite Cornell University horrified Americans. But when the alleged victim, known only as "Jane Doe", went public, she suffered a new kind of abuse, her lawyer told AFP.
The doxxing, threats and harassment targeting the woman, Thomas Giuffra said, expose a wider backlash against the MeToo movement, which prompted a societal reckoning with sexual abuse by men.
"I think we've gone the wrong way in how sexual assault is viewed in this country," said Giuffra, whose client claims that seven male students assaulted her at the Ivy League college in 2024.
"The message is to other survivors: Keep your mouth shut, or this is going to happen to you."
Giuffra cited a "swatting" incident in October in which police drew their guns at the woman's home after a man gave her address in a hoax call claiming to have shot his mother.
The lawyer also said he had received death threats.
"Somebody called my office and said 'drop the case, or I'm going to kill your wife'," he said in an interview at his 29th-floor Manhattan office.

Giuffra has previously represented accusers of Harvey Weinstein, the disgraced Hollywood mogul at the centre of abuse allegations that spurred the MeToo movement seeking to end impunity for sexual assault and rape.
"I thought we were moving in the right direction after MeToo, and there was just the backlash, and that set us back," he said, citing so-called "manosphere" influencers who oppose feminism.
In the Cornell backlash, he blamed "people who felt that the status quo was being threatened, people who didn't like the idea of women being treated equally, people who wanted to shut up women".
'Brave woman'
Despite the intimidation, Giuffra said his client wanted her lawsuit to transform how Cornell and other US universities deal with sexual assault.
An estimated one in four female students experience rape or sexual assault at some point during their undergraduate studies, according to a 2020 study by the Association of American Universities.
Fraternities — male social clubs common on US campuses — are particularly scrutinised. The men accused in the Cornell case belonged to one, and the alleged gang rape took place at a fraternity house.
"It's not just about money; it's also about effectuating some kind of change," Giuffra said, adding that any settlement with Cornell would include steps to "protect, educate, support students".

"I think she wants her story to be: I made a difference," Giuffra said. "Jane doesn't want some other woman, if God forbid this happens to them, to be left on their own, thrown overboard like she was."
Cornell has already announced several preliminary reforms to support sexual assault victims and commissioned an independent probe into how it responded in 2024.
Following her initial allegations, Cornell closed the fraternity and temporarily suspended the accused male students, two of whom were later expelled. Critics have said the response was too lenient.
On Friday, Cornell's faculty voted no-confidence in the university leadership.
New York's top prosecutor has also launched a fresh criminal investigation into the rape allegations after local authorities said they declined to prosecute in 2024 over a lack of evidence.
Giuffra praised the changes but said they were long overdue and inadequate. "There's an expression: that's a day late and a dollar short."
He said the accuser was still traumatised by her ordeal and had to take medication to help her sleep. Still, he praised her as a "brave woman".
"She's just trying to get through it every day at a time and trying to bring about some good," Giuffra said.

86ce07d3249ebc43: WASHINGTON: US president Donald Trump on Friday named Stephen Miller, architect of his hardline immigration policy, as his new chief of staff, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback after the Republicans' midterm hammering.
Ultra-loyalist Miller, 41, will replace Susie Wiles, who becomes the first major White House casualty from the Democratic landslide earlier this week.

Democrats pledged they would fight "every step of the way" against Miller, who became synonymous with scenes of masked immigration agents and violent confrontations in which federal agents shot dead two Americans.
"I wanted to make a change," Trump told reporters at the White House when asked why he had named Miller to replace Wiles.
"Sometimes in life you have to make moves."
Trump's move was particularly startling as he had repeatedly insisted before the midterms that there was "zero chance" of replacing Wiles.
A White House official told AFP that Wiles had resigned on Thursday night.

But naming the combative Miller was the clearest possible signal from Trump that the gloves are now off after his brief conciliatory gestures to Democrats in the wake of the Republican midterms collapse.
Known for his sharp suits and sunglasses, Miller has been one of Trump's closest aides for decades, pushing nativist policies that gelled with Trump's "America First" agenda.
As Trump's deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security advisor, he was the brains behind the mass deportation programme that defined the first year of the president's second term.
But he faced widespread criticism after the deadly shootings of two protesters by immigration agents in Minneapolis in January -- incidents that sparked mass demonstrations.
"Stephen Miller is the architect of the most barbaric, inhumane policies of this administration. Trump couldn't have made a worse choice," Minority Leader Chuck Schumer posted on X.
"Our Democratic majorities will fight him every step of the way,"
'It's Miller Time'
In a post on Truth Social earlier announcing Miller's appointment, Trump described him as "one of my most trusted advisors".
Trump said Wiles had "done an outstanding job" and would be "moving over to the Trump Political Operation. I want to thank her for her service as Chief of Staff -- She has done a great job!"
White House communications director Steven Cheung said Miller was a "Trump OG, someone who has been with the President since the very beginning.
"He will help the Administration deliver on monumental victories for the rest of this historic second term.
Top administration figures also praised Wiles, the first female White House chief of staff, whom Trump dubbed the "ice maiden" for maintaining discipline in the West Wing.
For most of the last two years, the 69-year-old had largely prevented the chaotic staff movements and infighting that marred Trump's first term.
But as the midterms loomed the writing was increasingly on the wall for Wiles, who announced recently that she had been given the all-clear from breast cancer.
"Serving President Trump in the White House has been the honor of a lifetime," Wiles said in a statement on X, adding that Friday would be her last day in her job.
"I'm so proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First."
Major figures in Trump's Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement -- reeling since the midterms -- hailed Miller's appointment.
"It's Miller Time," posted right-wing journalist Jack Posobiec, referring to a famous slogan for an American beer brand.
7050994d755c12b4: MELAKA: Campaigning for the Melaka polls has so far been marked by a relatively cordial atmosphere on the ground, even as political parties sharpen their rhetoric and step up efforts to secure support ahead of polling day on Nov 14.

Campaign workers from Barisan Nasional, Pakatan Harapan and Perikatan Nasional have described the campaign as largely peaceful, with candidates concentrating on meeting voters, visiting communities and presenting their respective agendas.
Some have even likened the contest to a friendly football match, suggesting that political differences have yet to translate into open hostility among campaign teams.
A campaign worker for BN's Serkam candidate Datuk Azman Abdullah said there had been no provocations, describing the campaign as a healthy contest.
"There has been no provocations. Everything is fine, and we are competing in a healthy manner. It is like a friendly match of football," he said.
He also claimed that some Pas supporters had expressed their intention to support Azman because they knew him personally, adding that the reception during house visits had been encouraging.
A PH campaign worker in Merlimau shared a similar assessment, saying candidates were focused on meeting people and visiting communities.

"There has been no provocation from rival parties because we regard this as a friendly match to choose the state's future leaders. The state election is a democratic process, and everyone is mature enough to carry out their responsibilities calmly," he said.

A PN Melaka media officer said he had received no complaints from the party's machinery about provocations, adding that cooperation between BN and PN supporters had improved, with both sides helping each other on the ground.

The coordination reflects efforts to translate the political understanding between the two coalitions into grassroots support, although local loyalties and competing interests could still pose challenges.

Universiti Teknologi Mara Faculty of Communication and Media Studies senior lecturer Dr Siti Faidul Maisarah Abdullah said the campaign was calmer than the two previous elections, with fewer controversies and party members displaying greater maturity and professionalism.
She also noted a change in campaign approaches, saying PH, which had appeared more aggressive in previous contests, was adopting a more persuasive approach this time.
Based on her observations, the authorities had been effective and committed in maintaining a harmonious atmosphere, which she said should be preserved until polling day.

Political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub similarly described the campaign as peaceful and orderly, with political competition yet to translate into widespread public hostility or major disturbances.

9acb70a939dbb976: KUALA LUMPUR: At least 26 people were arrested following two riots in the Klang Valley, with police also seizing several weapons.
In Kuala Lumpur, more than 400 people were detained in raids at two entertainment outlets, one involving drug-related offences and the other the operation of an unlicensed entertainment centre.
In Jerantut, Pahang, a Standard One pupil was allegedly sexually abused by his teacher as punishment for failing to complete his homework.
Here are some of the major crime cases reported this week.
POLICE NAB 26 IN TWO SEPARATE RIOTS
KUALA LUMPUR: Police detained 17 people following a brawl at the Lembah Jaya flats in Ampang, after videos of the incident went viral on social media.
Police were dispatched to the scene just after 2am on Oct 31, but found the situation calm.
However, police arrested 17 men from a group that had gathered at the location. They were detained to assist in investigations.
They were remanded for between two and three days. The case is being investigated for rioting while armed with deadly weapons.

In a separate incident, nine people, including a woman, were arrested following a riot outside a cafe in Desa Tun Razak, Sungai Besi, Kuala Lumpur, believed to have been triggered by a dispute over business territory.
The suspects were aged between 16 and 44. Preliminary police investigations revealed that the clash stemmed from a misunderstanding over control of the business area.
Six of those arrested had previous criminal and drug-related records.
Police also seized several items believed to have been used in the fight and are tracking down about 15 other people.
TWO PARANG ATTACKS LEAVE ONE DEAD AND ANOTHER INJURED
PASIR GUDANG: A man was seriously injured after being attacked by a group of men armed with parang outside an apartment building in Taman Cendana, Pasir Gudang, Johor, just after midnight on Nov 2.
Jealousy was believed to be the motive behind the attack.
Police arrested a man in his 30s and seized a parang believed to have been used in the attack.
The victim was taken to Hospital Pasir Gudang and was reported to be in stable condition.
The suspect, who had a record of eight previous criminal and drug-related offences, also tested positive for methamphetamine.
Meanwhile, in Banting, Selangor, a man in his 20s died after being attacked by a group of men armed with parang.
The motive was believed to be revenge.
Three men in their 30s were arrested in the Banting area to assist in investigations.
Police are investigating the case under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
TEACHER ARRESTED OVER SEXUAL ABUSE OF SEVEN-YEAR-OLD PUPIL

JERANTUT: A 24-year-old male teacher was arrested over allegations that he repeatedly sexually abused a seven-year-old pupil at a primary school here, including allegedly forcing the boy to perform oral sex as punishment for failing to complete his homework.
The alleged incidents reportedly took place in a science laboratory store.
Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob confirmed the arrest.
The case came to light after the boy disclosed the abuse to his family on Oct 27, prompting his father to lodge a police report.
The teacher was remanded for six days to facilitate investigations.
417 DETAINED IN NIGHTCLUB RAIDS
KUALA LUMPUR: Police detained 417 people during a raid on an unlicensed entertainment centre suspected of being linked to drug activities along Jalan Sultan Ismail here.
The raid was conducted on Nov 1 following intelligence that the premises was allegedly being used for drug-related activities.
Dang Wangi police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said those detained comprised security guards, workers and patrons, including four Bangladeshis.
The 417, comprising 299 men and 118 women, were taken to the Dang Wangi district police headquarters for documentation and urine screening.
In a separate operation conducted on the same day, police arrested eight men, aged between 21 and 40, at another unlicensed entertainment centre along Jalan Tun Razak.

Wangsa Maju police chief ACP Annas Sulaiman said those arrested comprised six foreigners, including two Bangladeshis and two Myanmar nationals without valid travel documents, as well as two Chinese nationals.
Police also seized audio equipment, four bottles of liquor and business sales receipts worth more than RM2,100.
THREE REMANDED FOR GIVING BRIBES IN CIGARETTE-SMUGGLING RING

The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) arrested three people, including a businessman with the title Datuk, for allegedly offering about RM1 million in bribes to police in exchange for protection for illegal cigarette-smuggling activities.
The suspects comprised a company owner and two women – a tuition teacher and a marketing executive – aged between their 30s and 50s.
They were arrested on Nov 1 at separate locations in Putrajaya, Selangor and Johor.

Preliminary investigations found that the suspects allegedly conspired to offer bribes to several police officers and lower-ranking policemen to prevent enforcement action against cigarette-smuggling activities in the East Coast states and the Klang Valley.
The alleged arrangement was believed to have been in operation since 2020, with the suspects also suspected of acting as intermediaries to channel the money to the police personnel involved.
MACC seized four luxury vehicles worth about RM600,000, four mobile phones and a laptop. It also froze 20 personal bank accounts and nine company accounts containing RM1.5 million.

efde793d332691e7: KUALA LUMPUR: An acquittal in a rape case, an order to undergo faith rehabilitation, fines for illegal racing under newly amended laws and unsuccessful court bids were among the court cases that made headlines across the country this week.
In Putrajaya, celebrity preacher Da'i Syed became a free man after succeeding in his final appeal against his rape conviction.

In Kuala Lumpur, a Taiwanese karaoke centre manager was charged with driving under the influence of drugs after allegedly crashing his car into a police escort rider attached to the entourage of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

Also in Kuala Lumpur, Toh Puan Na'imah Abdul Khalid, widow of the late Tun Daim Zainuddin, failed in her suit against Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over a police probe into an alleged plot to topple the government.
Here are several court cases that made headlines this week.
PREACHER DA'I SYED WINS APPEAL
Celebrity preacher Da'i Syed, whose real name is Syed Shah Iqmal Syed Mohd Shaiful, was cleared of raping a 23-year-old woman in Shah Alam in 2019.

In a 2-1 majority decision, Court of Appeal judges Datuk Azman Abdullah, who chaired the panel, and Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid allowed Syed Shah Iqmal's final appeal, while Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid dissented.
The bench set aside the 10-year jail term and three strokes of the rotan imposed by the High Court.
Azman said the defence had succeeded in raising reasonable doubt, rendering Syed Shah Iqmal's conviction unsafe.
On Dec 10, 2020, Syed Shah Iqmal pleaded not guilty to raping the woman in a condominium in i-City, Section 7, on Sept 11, 2019.
The charge, framed under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
In 2023, the Shah Alam Sessions Court acquitted him after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case.
However, the Shah Alam High Court allowed the prosecution's appeal and ordered him to enter his defence.
On Aug 30, 2024, Sessions Court judge Adlin Abdul Majid sentenced him to 10 years in jail and three strokes of the rotan.
TAIWANESE MAN CHARGED OVER CRASH THAT INJURED POLICEMAN

Taiwanese karaoke centre manager Wei Fu-Chun, 52, pleaded not guilty at the magistrate's court to driving a Mercedes-Benz under the influence of drugs and crashing into Corporal Samsul Rahimi Sapari, 42, who sustained injuries to his legs and hands.
The offence took place at 8.50pm along Jalan Tun Sambanthan on Oct 31.
He was charged under Section 44(1A)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a jail term of between seven and 10 years and a fine of between RM30,000 and RM50,000 upon conviction.

Samsul, who is attached to the city Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department's motorcycle unit, was returning from escort duty with the entourage of Negri Sembilan Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Magistrate Aliaa Anwar denied Wei bail and fixed Jan 6 for the submission of documents.
A breathalyser test conducted on Wei returned a negative result for alcohol, but drugs believed to be ecstasy were found in the car.
NA'IMAH AND SONS' SUIT AGAINST PRIME MINISTER STRUCK OUT

The originating summons filed by Toh Puan Na'imah Abdul Khalid, her two sons and two lawyers challenging police investigations into an alleged plot to topple the government was struck out by the High Court.
The suit was filed by Na'imah, widow of the late Tun Daim Zainuddin, alongside Amir Zainuddin, Amin Zainuddin and lawyers Amir Zharif Abdullah and Muhammad Nizamuddin Abdul Hamid.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Mohd Khalid Ismail and the government were named as the defendants.
Judge Indra Nehru Savandiah ruled that there was no cogent evidence to substantiate allegations that the police investigation was conducted in bad faith or with mala fide intentions.

She said the allegations that the ongoing police investigation might have been influenced by the first defendant's alleged public comments were merely assertions or assumptions unsupported by facts capable of establishing bad faith or mala fide intentions.
She also said there was no nexus linking the first defendant's alleged public comments to the independent ongoing investigation, which was based on a police report.

The plaintiffs contended that the investigation under Section 124B of the Penal Code for activities detrimental to parliamentary democracy constituted an abuse of statutory power and was initiated in bad faith.

They sought, among other things, a declaration that the investigation by the IGP and the government under Section 124B was unlawful, unconstitutional, tainted with bad faith, carried out for ulterior purposes and an abuse of statutory power.
MAN ORDERED TO UNDERGO THREE MONTHS OF FAITH REHABILITATION
A man who went viral for performing a non-Islamic ritual was ordered by the Syariah Lower Court to undergo three months of faith rehabilitation after pleading guilty to a charge of improper worship.
Syariah judge Mohd Faizal Habib ordered Aliff Daniel Adli, 21, to undergo rehabilitation at the Baitul Iman Faith Rehabilitation Centre in Ulu Yam instead of serving a jail term or paying a fine.
Aliff admitted to committing improper worship by holding a religious object, performing a ritual involving body piercing and kneeling with both hands clasped against his chest in front of a statue.
The offence took place at a temple in Batu Caves between 9pm and 11pm on Jan 24, 2024.
The court reprimanded Aliff, saying the offence was not merely a breach of written law but a serious transgression. It also advised him to repent.
SINGAPOREAN AMONG THREE FINED FOR ILLEGAL RACING
Singaporean national serviceman Syajahan Alfian Abdullah was fined RM3,500 by the Johor Bahru magistrate's court for riding a motorcycle at high speed and taking part in a speed challenge.

The charge was brought against Syajahan, 19, under Section 42A(2) of the amended Road Transport Act 1987 (Amendment) 2026, which criminalises illegal racing and speed testing on public roads. The amendments came into force on Oct 16.
He pleaded guilty to committing the act at Km12.5 of the Second Link Expressway southbound in Iskandar Puteri at 2.10am on Oct 18.

Two other local youths, Muhammad Daniel Hakim Mohamad Rashid, 24, and Gonzales Mckhovic George, 18, were also fined RM3,500 each after pleading guilty to offences under Section 42A(1) for racing their motorcycles along different stretches of the same expressway at the same time and date.
The amended provisions carry a fine of between RM2,000 and RM10,000, a jail term of up to two years, or both, for a first offence.
The three paid their fines.
CAPRICE ORDERED TO PAY PREACHER EBIT LEW RM220,000 FOR DEFAMATION
The Shah Alam Sessions Court ordered rapper and influencer Ariz Ramli, better known as Caprice, to pay preacher Ebit Lew RM220,000 in damages for defamation.
On Nov 2, judge Zuhrina Mohamed Nor ordered Caprice to deposit the sum into the account of Ebit's lawyers and pay RM2,000 in costs after dismissing his application to stay the payment.
In August, the judge had ordered Caprice to apologise and pay Ebit RM220,000 after finding that he had defamed the preacher in 2023.
Caprice was also ordered to remove seven statements made alongside Indonesian influencer Mondy Tattoo within 48 hours and barred from making further comments or statements about Ebit.
The case stemmed from a video Caprice uploaded on Sept 15, 2023, featuring Mondy as a guest.
Ebit said the video implied that he had sexually harassed and taken advantage of Mondy, portraying him as irresponsible and someone who exploited religion.
