a85f9b6a75e39be3: The DRC is in the seventh month of an Ebola outbreak. AP Photo/Sebastien Kitsa MusayiI visited a family of 19 in Sierra Leone in 2015. By the time I arrived, eight had died. The other 11 were left to live with the grief and fear of what might happen next. I am a medical doctor and epidemiologist, and at that time I was serving on an African Union Ebola response mission. The 2014-16 epidemic in West Africa caused more than 28,600 cases and 11,300 deaths. Over roughly six months in Sierra Leone, I saw how quickly the disease could overwhelm families and health services. That’s also when I learned that good medical advice can fail if people do not trust those delivering it. Some families buried relatives secretly, despite warnings. In certain communities, funeral practices included washing the body and sprinkling water on mourners, which risked exposing people to infected bodily fluids. Simply repeating instructions did not help. But those of us working in the field found that working with families to make burials safer while respecting their grief helped them to mourn their loss while stopping the virus from spreading. More than a decade later, those experiences have returned to my mind. The Ebola outbreak now sweeping across parts of Central Africa is different from the one I responded to. Still, one lesson remains: Timely international support makes a huge difference. A growing outbreak The current outbreak was declared in the Democratic Republic of Congo, or DRC, in May 2026. By Oct. 28, 2026, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 10,305 confirmed cases and 4,996 deaths across five countries, with new updates daily. The DRC accounts for nearly all of those cases and deaths. This is already the second-largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded, after the 2014-16 epidemic. The current outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, whereas the 2014-16 epidemic involved a different Ebola virus. No vaccine or specific treatment is currently approved for Bundibugyo. The World Health Organization warns that late detection, deaths outside health facilities and sustained transmission in the DRC remain serious concerns. The DRC has extensive experience with responding to outbreaks, and African institutions are coordinating a continental response. Africa has the expertise and leadership. What it needs right now is sustained support that reaches the front line – quickly, safely and accountably. Crossing borders Ebola follows human movement. In October, Kenya reported infections linked to a traveler who had passed through Uganda from the DRC. Nigeria also reported an imported case around the same time. Symptoms can appear between two and 21 days after exposure, and people are generally not infectious before symptoms begin. A traveler may therefore pass a temperature check and become ill days later. These events show why countries need to share information quickly, verify travel histories and maintain contact tracing across borders. In response to the 2014 Ebola outbreak, American healthcare workers set up makeshift clinics like this one outside Monrovia, Liberia. Abbas Dulleh/AP What international support looks like now International partners are, in fact, contributing. In September 2026, the United States reported US$887 million in Ebola-related health and humanitarian assistance. The U.K. announced a contribution of roughly £78 million ($104 million). In October, the World Bank described $426.6 million in current and planned financing for the DRC and neighboring countries. And Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention reported nearly $3 billion in international pledges following a September mobilization effort. But pledges are not the same as supplies delivered or services provided, and these contributions are coming late in the outbreak. In 2014, Britain helped expand treatment and safe-burial operations in Sierra Leone. The U.S. mobilized logistics capacity in Liberia, while France assisted Guinea. And African Union health workers served alongside local teams and other partners. That cooperation saved lives, though the global response was slow to scale up. It has been discouraging for me to see that today’s response has not built on that experience without waiting for the outbreak to grow further. According to the WHO, massive cuts to international aid over the past year diminished a quicker response. The success of international collaboration will be measured in how many contacts are reached, how rapidly patients are tested, how many health workers have protective equipment and are consistently paid, whether women can still deliver babies safely, and whether remote communities can get care. Building connections with everyday people My experience in Sierra Leone in 2014 taught me that trust is essential to outbreak control. Families need credible explanations, timely information and opportunities to ask questions. Local health workers, faith leaders, survivors and community organizations can help bridge the gap between an emergency response and the people it seeks to protect. That gap can be large even when a disease is widely known. A colleague and I conducted a study involving 440 secondary school students in Nigeria in 2014, and we found that 95.4% had heard of Ebola. Yet only 42.3% identified fever as a possible symptom, and only 33.2% recognized the risk associated with certain burial practices. Seeing that awareness of the disease alone was not enough, we subsequently began Ebola education activities in local Nigerian schools. The need for reliable information from trusted sources remains in 2026. Risk messages must be consistent, culturally sensitive and practical. This works only when communities are partners in recognizing illness, seeking early care, contact follow-up and safe, dignified burials. Even in times of emergency, health workers cannot treat communities simply as audiences for instructions. Reaching affected communities In August 2026, Africa CDC and the WHO jointly called for expanded laboratory and treatment capacity and faster delivery of supplies. But in the DRC, insecurity and displacement due to ongoing conflict, in addition to poor roads, can prevent supplies and patients from reaching treatment centers. These obstacles may also keep laboratories from receiving samples and contact-tracing teams from visiting households. The ministry of health is not equipped to resolve these problems. The response therefore requires cooperation among health authorities, humanitarian agencies, local government, transport services and those responsible for civilian safety. There are signs that investments in these services are helping. In October, the World Bank reported that supported detection timelines in the DRC had improved. This meant new cases were being detected within one or two days by September, a huge improvement from the 10-day detection timeline early in the outbreak. The Tumaini vaccine trials started in the DRC at the end of October 2026. ‘Tumaini’ is the Swahili word for hope. AP Photo/Dieudonne Dirole Looking to the future Because Bundibugyo virus lacks an approved vaccine or specific treatment, this outbreak also demands carefully conducted research. The Tumaini vaccine trial, begun in Bunia, DRC, in October 2026, is an important step toward a potential vaccine. The hope is that this effort will prevent more families from experiencing loss. I still remember the 11 survivors in that Sierra Leone household I visited back in 2015. I never learned what ultimately happened to them, but more than a decade later, I still think about them. Olayinka Stephen Ilesanmi was the past West Africa Regional Program Lead for Africa CDC.
d7875be231db7976: People who have lived most of their lives blind often have extraordinary hearing abilities. In new research published in the Journal of Neuroscience, my colleagues and I discovered that this ability arises from how their auditory systems are able to more consistently and reliably process sounds compared with people who aren’t blind. And interestingly, sighted musicians seem to enhance their hearing through a similar mechanism. Hearing is a complicated process. It involves many stages, starting from how the ears detect sounds and going all the way up to how the brain extracts meaningful information from those sounds. Different mechanisms are involved, too. You can get better at hearing by being more selective or more consistent. Think of writing the letter “A.” You can practice to make your “A” either more distinguishable from “B” or look more similar to other “A’s” every time you write it. The latter is called internal noise – how consistently your auditory system responds to the same sound over time. The less internal noise you have, the more reliably you can tell similar sounds apart. How does your brain pick out the voice of someone you know from the crowd? Seth Joel/DigitalVision via Getty Images We recruited nine individuals who became blind before the age of 2 and 18 sighted individuals. Participants in both groups had varying levels of musical training, giving us an opportunity to examine how musical experience can also affect hearing abilities. Participants completed two simple hearing tasks. In one task, they detected a tone presented in background noise, which allowed us to assess how the cochlea in the inner ear processes different sound frequencies. In the other task, they judged which of the two tones had a higher pitch, a task that also relies on how the brain interprets sound information. We found that people with early-life blindness were better than sighted people only in the pitch discrimination task. This means that their improved hearing abilities may selectively originate from changes in how their brains process auditory information and not from how their ears detect sounds. Importantly, we used a mathematical model to better understand what drives differences in pitch discrimination. The model showed that the enhanced ability to tell pitches apart in people with early-life blindness happens by reducing internal noise: more consistent and reliable processing of sounds rather than greater selectivity for different sound frequencies. Surprisingly, we found that musical training seems to similarly reduce internal noise. Sighted musicians also responded to sounds more consistently compared with people who neither experienced early-life blindness nor received extensive musical training. Why it matters Because your brain doesn’t know what kind of sensory environment it’ll encounter when you’re born, it’s equipped with a special ability: to tune its responses to parts of the world that matter to it. This ability helps people see, hear and master new skills as their experiences change, like when children learn to read and when adults learn to identify different bird species. Words and birds have become a meaningful part of their experiences, so their brains are tuned to the new information. Our study identifies internal noise as an important factor that facilitates this brain plasticity. There are many ways a person can come to have reduced levels of internal noise, and one is by building a more accurate template for perceiving the world. It is possible that sensory experience, whether it be being blind or being a musician, might help create and fine-tune the perceptual template relevant for hearing. People with musical training also process sound more consistently than people without training. Jose Luis Pelaez Inc/DigitalVision via Getty Images What still isn’t known If sensory experiences and training can tap into the brain’s ability to adapt, researchers may be able to use them to improve perceptual abilities. For example, targeted training to hear sound locations could help people who are beginning to lose vision learn to rely on other senses to navigate. However, researchers still don’t know how much training is needed and what aspects of the auditory experience are key to drive behaviorally meaningful changes in the brain. Another important question is whether and how this brain plasticity varies depending on when someone loses their vision or begins musical training. The brain might have greater plasticity early in development, and how sensory experiences shape the brain may differ in adulthood. What’s next How far can people push their ability to learn? Can everyone become super listeners with training? If the brain’s plasticity is limited in adulthood, are there ways to reopen the door? And what role does internal noise play in this learning? Moving forward, our team is interested in understanding whether the enhanced pitch discrimination we saw in people with early-life blindness and sighted musicians extends to more complex, everyday listening. The Research Brief is a short take about interesting academic work. Woon Ju Park receives funding from NIH and the Georgia Institute of Technology Smithgall-Watts Early Career Award.

One more thing
Meet the radio-obsessed civilian shaping Ukraine’s drone defense

Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov is, at least unofficially, a spy. Once a month, he drives to the frontline in a VW van equipped with radio hardware, roof antennas, and devices that monitor drones. Over several days, he searches the skies for transmissions that can help Ukrainian troops.

Drones define this brutal conflict, and most rely on the radio communications Flash has obsessed over since childhood. Though now a civilian, the former officer has taken it upon himself to inform his country’s defense on all matters related to radio.

Unlike traditional spies, Flash shares his discoveries with over 127,000 followers—including soldiers and officials—on social media. His work has won fans in the military, but also sparked controversy among the top brass. Read the full story.
—Charlie Metcalfe

d3e82c516963b892: From Hartini Zainudin
I am dismayed! I read an FMT report about a young man and his biological father who lost their citizenship case.

A Malaysian father went to the Kota Bharu High Court with a DNA report from our own chemistry department proving the young man beside him is his son. To add insult to injury, he left with an order to pay the government RM4,000!
The son was born in Golok in June 2006 and was carried across the border at three months old. He has lived here for 20 years. He has no birth certificate and no nationality anywhere in the world.
The court ruled that because his parents could not prove they were married when he was born, the law must look past his Malaysian father entirely and treat him as the child of his Thai mother alone.
I read the news report and I am still angry; it is outrageous.

In fairness to the judicial commissioner, he applied the law as it stands. Section 17 of Part III of the Second Schedule of the Federal Constitution states that for a child born out of wedlock, any reference to the father is read as a reference to the mother.
The Federal Court confirmed this in the 2021 landmark case CTEB & Anor v Ketua Pengarah Pendaftaran Negara, on almost identical facts: a Malaysian father, a Thai mother, no registered marriage.
Citizenship by operation of law is fixed at the moment of birth, and nothing that happens afterwards can change it.
So the fault lies with the law, and with those of us who have left it standing. Whatever its purpose in 1957, the rule now overrides a laboratory result that settles paternity beyond doubt.
Our own government chemist confirmed who this boy's father is. Our own constitution then told the court to ignore him.

I have spent close to 20 years recovering abandoned babies, sitting with young mothers once they are traced, and working with children in detention. I know how a birth goes unregistered. The clinic across the border is closer. The couple married in a religious ceremony and never registered it. Someone told the father the paperwork would cost money he did not have, or get him into trouble. The child made none of these choices ... none!

The child carries the consequences for life anyway. No identity card, no exam certificate in his own name, no legal job, no passport, no registered marriage. When he has children of his own, the problem passes to them. Statelessness is inherited. How is what’s happening to him his fault?

This is far from a rare case. The national registration department (JPN) registered 542,363 births of children born out of wedlock between 2006 and June 2017, the most recent national figure on record.
We have no count of how many have a Malaysian father who wants to claim them. The law has never asked.

The court says this young man should look to his mother's nationality. He left Thailand as an infant with no birth record. Anyone who has tried to obtain documents from a country they cannot remember, with nothing to prove they were born there, knows what that answer is worth.
We fought hard to protect foundlings and the overseas-born children of Malaysian mothers. The children of unmarried Malaysian fathers are still waiting. Four things would change that:
Amend Section 17. A Malaysian parent, mother or father, married or not, should be able to pass on citizenship where parentage is proven, including by DNA.

Use Article 15A properly. The home ministry should publish clear criteria and timelines for registering children like this one, treat a chemistry department DNA report as sufficient proof, and give written reasons for every refusal.
Stop pursuing costs against stateless applicants. A young man with no nationality should never be billed RM4,000 for asking the court who he is.
Make late birth registration reachable. Border births, unregistered marriages and families afraid of the system need a simple, safe route to register, years later if necessary.
A father stood up in court and did the honourable thing by saying: this is my son, and here is the proof. Most of us would call that responsibility. Our law called it irrelevant.
Until Parliament fixes Section 17, I hope the home minister asks for this file and grants this young man what the court could not. He has waited 20 years already.
Hartini Zainudin is co-founder of Yayasan Chow Kit, founder of Kasih Madhya, and co-founder of Voice of the Children.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
4513cd1ca7d87aeb: Humanoid robots remain unproven at scale and have not yet achieved widespread commercialization, compared with industrial robots that have decades of proven track records in warehouses and factories. That frank acknowledgment is among the risks outlined in a securities filing by Agility Robotics—the first dedicated developer of humanoid robots to become a publicly traded company in the United States.

The robotics company, headquartered in Salem, Oregon, previously became the first to achieve full-time commercial deployment of humanoid robots at a customer warehouse in 2024. Now, Agility’s public listing on the Nasdaq stock exchange as of November 5 has come with financial disclosures detailing how the company plans to build a business around renting out or selling humanoid robots to perform manual labor.

“When we are doing robots as a service, it is much lower risk for customers to use it because they are getting a return on investment on day one,” Jonathan Hurst, co-founder and chief robot officer at Agility Robotics, told Ars. "Because they're paying a rate that is comparable to the human labor rate, and that makes the economics pretty straightforward.”
31a0ef2c2c5cd3a3: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The ringgit extended its gains against the US dollar and other major currencies on Thursday, closing firmer following Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) decision to maintain the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent.
The decision was made during the central bank’s final Monetary Policy Committee meeting of the year today.
At 6pm, the local note rose to 4.0445/0490 versus the greenback from Wednesday’s close of 4.0610/0660.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the decision to keep the OPR unchanged at 2.75 per cent was in line with estimates.
He said BNM is seen to be positive about the current state of the economy, with the 2026 gross domestic product (GDP) growth expected to settle above 5.0 per cent.
“At the same time, the balance of risks are seen to be stable although concerns on higher inflation going forward warrant a cautious stance.

“On that note, the case for a 25-basis point hike in OPR during 2027 should not be ruled out and perhaps it could happen in the first quarter of 2027. As such, this could provide further support to the ringgit,” he told Bernama.

Mohd Afzanizam also said the US midterm elections were a key driver of market sentiment today as a Democrats-controlled Congress could mean more scrutiny on President Donald Trump administration’s policies.
“Consequently, Brent crude oil fell below US$100 (RM404.57) per barrel to US$95.12 per barrel currently, while the US Dollar Index (DXY) fell by 0.14 per cent to 101.423 points,” he said.

Meanwhile, SPI Asset Management managing partner Stephen Innes said market sentiment was also supported by a decline in US Treasury yields following the sharp overnight drop in crude oil prices, as the geopolitical risk premium was effectively stripped from the oil market.
He said traders were increasingly convinced that a return to conflict with Iran was unlikely, easing inflationary concerns in the US bond market.

“The currency is taking its cues from external developments rather than domestic monetary policy. That said, the US dollar has not weakened significantly, and I expect that's because the US Federal Reserve (Fed) is still expected to raise rates in December.

“Until those expectations begin to unwind, there's probably a limit to how far the ringgit can appreciate. For now, the direction of crude oil prices and the Fed's reaction function as the two big moving parts for Asian currencies, including the ringgit,” he added.
The ringgit traded higher against a basket of major currencies.

It strengthened versus the Japanese yen to 2.5548/5578 from 2.5636/5669 at Wednesday’s close, appreciated against the euro to 4.5428/5478 from 4.5723/5779 yesterday, and edged up vis-a-vis the British pound to 5.4455/4516 from 5.4783/4850 previously.
However, the ringgit performed mostly lower against its Asean peers.

The local currency gained versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1679/1717 from the previous close of 3.1771/1813, but it slipped against the Thai baht to 12.1013/1199 from 12.0673/0868 yesterday, inched down versus the rupiah to 223.6/224.0 from 223.5/223.8, and fell vis-a-vis the Philippine peso to 6.42/6.43 from 6.39/6.40. — Bernama

aa77b635d887aeb9: A sweeping bit of legislation designed to cut red tape could speed up the buildout of energy infrastructure in the US.

With the dust barely settled on this week’s momentous midterms, the Senate is set to vote on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) on November 9. It’s a plan that could finally start an overhaul of the slow, complicated process for getting energy projects approved, as part of something called permitting reform. People on both sides of the political aisle have been pushing for this type of change for some years.
The key question is whether this will cut greenhouse-gas emissions from the US energy sector or push them higher still.

The federal permitting system is designed to protect the environment against industrial pollution from large projects like power plants, transmission lines, and natural-gas pipelines. Today, permitting is governed by a range of laws, including the National Environmental Policy Act and the Clean Water Act. And if there’s one thing you might know about the current state of permitting in the US it’s that it’s slow and incredibly complicated.

So in its 417 pages, BAAJA attempts to tighten things up. The bill has provisions that narrow the sorts of projects that need to apply for federal permits and others that enact deadlines in hopes of speeding up a process that today can take years. (There are also specific provisions about transmission planning, mining, and the rest of the kitchen sink; this thing is dense.)

One thing to know about this bill is that it’s largely technology neutral: It opens the doors for the buildout of projects involving both fossil fuels and renewables. So there’s a weird mishmash of legislators and outside groups supporting it.

The bill’s four sponsors in the Senate are two Republicans and two Democrats. The White House has backed this permitting reform bill, with its Council of Economic Advisors finding that it would reduce review times and have economic benefits like boosting GDP.

Clean energy groups like the American Clean Power Association have largely come out in favor of the bill too, with the group’s analysis finding that it could unlock 350 gigawatts of new clean energy for the grid.

Some environmental groups, however, oppose the bill, or parts of it. An assessment from the Natural Resources Defense Council says the parts about transmission could have substantial benefits for the grid, but the narrowing of environmental reviews could be damaging for public and private lands.

Many in the climate world have long been calling for permitting reform, arguing that renewables stand to benefit more than fossil fuels. The thinking is that solar and wind power are some of the cheapest sources available today, so if we unlock the ability to build more energy, they are likely to win out economically.

A few early analyses have tried to quantify just what BAAJA would mean for emissions in the US. One, from the think tank Rhodium Group, found that in the best-case scenario, the bill would cut economy-wide emissions by 4%, reduce annual energy bills by $78 per household, and add 200 gigawatts of new clean energy by 2040. In the worst case, emissions would stay about the same.

Another report, from the nonprofit research group Resources for the Future, found that the bill could cut power-sector emissions 6% by 2041 and save more than $350 billion on system costs by midcentury.

But there are some concerns that this permitting bill’s real effect would be to open the floodgates for new natural-gas plants. As data centers have put more pressure on the grid, a wave of such plants have been announced.

“You get down to a trade-off between essentially growing the clean electricity industry on the one hand and then, as a compromise, growing the fossil-fuel industry on the other,” says Kevin Kircher, an energy modeler and assistant professor of mechanical engineering at Purdue.

To quantify that trade-off, Kircher also modeled the potential emissions effects of the bill and found that if BAAJA had been in place in 2025, energy sector emissions would have been higher than the actual baseline. Health and mortality risks associated with air pollution would also have increased.

This bill is scheduled for a Senate vote on November 9, well before the next Congress takes control. It’s not clear what the dramatic victories for Democrats might mean for the legislation, which was expected to pass the Senate with largely Republican support if a few Democrats got on board. Democrats could decide to wait for next year, when they’ll have control of both chambers. But any deal would ultimately need to win Trump’s signature, limiting what a future bill might be able to change.

In a world where permitting new projects is easier, we’ll see more clean energy, but we’ll see more natural gas, too. And while prices could get lower, that could push demand for electricity higher, leading to more emissions overall.
Simplifying the permitting system and cutting red tape is a worthy goal. But when it comes to emissions, it still really matters what, exactly, you want to build.
ada58846ea285577: TOKYO, Nov 5 — Japanese gaming giant Nintendo reported a drop in quarterly net profit today as unit sales slowed for its Switch 2 console, but maintained its annual forecasts.
A remake of 1990s action-adventure classic The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which comes out today has sparked nostalgic fan excitement.
But market analysts will be watching to see how much the title can boost sales of the Switch 2, which became the world’s fastest-selling games console on its 2025 release.
Nintendo reported an 11 per cent year-on-year rise in net profit for the first half of 2026-27.
But in the second quarter, from July-September, net profit was down 29 per cent to 73.5 billion yen (US$465.3 million) -- missing estimates of 82.2 billion yen in a Bloomberg survey of analysts.
The company maintained its annual net profit forecast of 310 billion yen.

“Although sales declined year-on-year due to lower hardware unit sales, operating profit rose” nearly 50 per cent in the first six months, due to steady sales of games and a windfall connected to US tariff refunds, Nintendo said.
The company sold nearly 6.5 million Switch 2 consoles in the first half, down from nearly 10.4 million the previous year, when the gadget was new.
This year Nintendo raised the price of Switch 2, as the global artificial intelligence boom causes the price of memory chips used in everyday electronics to soar.
Memory chip shortage
Some analysts have also said the lack of any blockbuster title to boost Switch 2 adoption among gamers has led to sluggish sales of the console.

“While working to bring Nintendo Switch 2 to more consumers, we will also leverage the Nintendo Switch hardware installed base and rich software lineup to expand software sales and maintain engagement,” the company said Thursday.
Nintendo’s latest addition to its long-running Zelda series, “Ocarina of Time”, is being released gradually across the world as part of the 40th anniversary of the saga.
It has already garnered widespread praise with a score of 96 out of 100 on aggregator site Metacritic by the eve of its release, putting it among the best-reviewed titles of the year so far.
Sony raises forecast
Sony upgraded its annual earnings forecast for the current fiscal year today thanks to robust sales of its games, music and movies.
The firm now expects to earn 1.33 trillion yen for the year to March, up from the previous upgraded forecast of 1.21 trillion issued in July.
The Japanese tech-entertainment conglomerate said second-quarter net profit jumped 44 percent to 449.6 billion yen, driven largely by games and films.
For the game operations, sales were helped by favourable foreign exchange rates but also strong sales of new titles.
In the movie segment, it noted an “increase in theatrical revenues primarily due to the contribution of ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’”.
The film was released in July and was a blockbuster success.
The game segment is also expected to benefit from the eagerly awaited November launch of “Grand Theft Auto VI”, which is predicted to be the biggest release in gaming for years. — AFP

The letter said the vessel had loaded about 35,432 tonnes of palm oil products at Dumai, Indonesia, before taking on a further 4,999.715 tonnes of Malaysian crude palm olein at Port Klang for shipment to Adabiya, Egypt.

It said the Indonesian outward manifest and accompanying documents described the cargo as refined palm oil products, including refined palm olein, refined, bleached and deodorised (RBD) palm oil, RBD palm stearin and RBD palm kernel oil.

However, Maritime Network said it later received information raising questions over whether the Malaysian crude palm olein had been commingled with the Indonesian cargo, and whether the actual grade of certain Indonesian products matched their descriptions in the shipping documents.
The LOD acknowledged that the precise nature, composition, timing and extent of any alleged commingling remained subject to documentary verification.

It also referred to WhatsApp correspondence dated October 16, in which an Olam Global Agri representative allegedly claimed to have previously spoken to Maritime Network and informed it that the cargo was crude.

The law firm said its client disputed that the correspondence established prior notification or informed consent, adding that no contemporaneous written notification or documentary evidence of such consent had been produced.
The LOD sought details of the alleged communication, including the persons involved, the date and time, the information disclosed and the terms of any purported agreement or approval.

It also referred to emails dated October 19 and 23, in which Olam Global Agri’s representative reportedly said the company had bought the Malaysian cargo from Mewah Oils Sdn Bhd on free-on-board (FOB) terms and was not the exporter of record.
The law firm said its client was not suggesting that Olam Global Agri had automatically assumed the exporter’s statutory obligations by buying the cargo on FOB terms.
However, it maintained that the company’s involvement in the vessel’s chartering arrangements, and any instructions on loading, stowage, commingling and documentation, required clarification.

Among the documents sought were cargo quality certificates, certificates of analysis, stowage plans, quantity measurement records, surveyor reports and communications involving the vessel’s master, owner, terminal operators and shipping agents.

The LOD also cited Regulation 12 of the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (Quality) Regulations 2005, including Regulation 12(3)©, which concerns the disclosure of the ingredients and composition of blended oil palm products in relevant commercial and shipping documents, where applicable.

The law firm said its client was not making a final determination on whether any regulatory breach had occurred, adding that the matter would have to be assessed by the competent authorities based on the evidence.

Olam Global Agri was given seven days from receipt of the LOD to provide documentary evidence supporting its position on prior notification and consent, or to withdraw the allegation if it could not be substantiated.
The LOD also sought an indemnity against specified claims and losses to the extent they are attributable to the company’s conduct, and reserved Maritime Network’s right to pursue legal remedies.

cf403874a276142d: Chinese women are challenging marriage pressures and redefining what it means to be single.
The marriage market at People’s Park in Shanghai, 2013. Photo by Jpbowen via Wikimedia Commons, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

On weekends at Shanghai’s People’s Park, umbrellas covered with handwritten sheets of paper line the paths. Parents stand beside them, exchanging information about their unmarried children: age, height, education, income, and whether they own an apartment. It is one of China’s most famous marriage markets — a place where private hopes and social expectations meet in public since 2005.
For years, the word shengnü (剩女), literally translated as “leftover women,” hovered over many of the women whose profiles appeared there.

The translation sounds strange in English because the original Chinese carries a sharper meaning. The character sheng (剩) does not simply mean “remaining.” It suggests something left behind, something unused. In everyday contexts, it can describe leftover food — something that has passed its ideal moment and may eventually be discarded.

When the term became popular in China in the late 2000s, it was used to describe unmarried urban women, often highly educated professionals, who were considered “too old” for marriage after their late twenties. The label was not just a description of marital status. It turned a personal choice into a social judgment.

But today, if you search Chinese media, the phrase shengnü appears far less frequently than it once did. Instead, a more neutral term, zhonggnü (中女), literally translated as “middle or in-and-between women,” is now more often used to describe unmarried women in their thirties in both mainstream media and social platforms.

While the word has faded, many of the expectations behind it remain. The language around unmarried women has become more circumspect, though still pointed. Instead of openly calling women “leftover,” conversations often appear in softer forms: concerns about women being “too picky,” warnings about missing the “best age” for marriage and childbirth, or questions about why a successful woman still has not found a partner.

Instead of using the neutral term zhonggnü, which still highlights women’s age, some women have created new terms and spaces on social media platforms, such as Xiaohongshu and Douban, to discuss these pressures on their own terms. For example, they have reframed the marriage debate to cuīhūn (催婚) — the repeated pressure from family members to marry — and kǒnghūn (恐婚) — the fear or hesitation surrounding marriage itself.
These words reveal a shift. The conversation is no longer only about why women are failing to meet expectations. Increasingly, women are asking whether those expectations should be followed at all.

On Xiaohongshu, a user writing under the name “十元尼美” (Ten Yuan Nimei) described seven years of pressure to marry, beginning when she graduated from university. By 30, she wrote, the pressure had eased — not because her family had accepted her choices, but because people arranging introductions considered her too old for the matchmaking market. At 34, she said, her parents had almost stopped asking.

Her advice to other women began with creating physical distance. Moving from her home province of Hunan to Beijing had largely confined her parents’ pressure to phone calls; later, she moved to Spain. “Sometimes, freedom comes not from persuasion, but from distance,” she wrote.

Other posts question the pressure itself. One shared by the account “渭北春天树” carried the title —“Pressuring someone to marry is, at its core, a form of expulsion.” (催婚的本质是一种驱逐) These conversations no longer see shengnü or unmarried women as a problem, but are turning the conversation on its head to scrutinize traditional conservative family values.

Some women have even embraced and reclaimed the characterization of shengnü as a form of empowerment. Online, some social media posts explicitly recast the label through a play on Chinese characters: 剩, meaning “leftover,” becomes 胜, meaning “victorious,” with the same pronunciation, shèng. A Xiaohongshu post shared by an account named “Kevin” declares: “I’m not a ‘leftover woman’; I’m a ‘victorious woman.’” It advocates remaining single rather than settling, pursuing personal growth, and enjoying time alone.

In another post, the creator “小李存钱记” addresses her mother’s worries about her being unmarried at 30. “I’m not a leftover woman! I’m a victorious woman!” reads the text across the image. She describes juggling several jobs and building an online following, presenting her work and earnings as evidence of her worth. The reframing rejects marriage as the measure of success, while placing considerable emphasis on professional achievement and financial independence.

These posts do not erase the social stigma of the term shengnü. Rather, they show how users are challenging the label by questioning family pressure, sharing ways to escape it, or replacing “leftover” with “victorious.” Yet the language of victory raises another question. If an unmarried woman must point to her earnings, career, or independence to defend her choices, how much room is there simply to be single?
16de4ca3c25d3eed: In an emergency, a human might someday ask a robotic assistant to fetch a wall-mounted defibrillator located down the hall. But if the robot has incorrectly labeled the defibrillator as a fire extinguisher in its stored memory, it may not know where to find the life-saving device. This robotic assistant could benefit from a new memory system created by MIT researchers. The system identifies entries in a robot’s memory that might be wrong and corrects the descriptions of mislabeled objects.  In the future, this method could make household or industrial robots better able to perform complex, multistep tasks, such as clearing a dining room table or working alongside human collaborators to assemble a piece of machinery.  Called UQ-DAAAM (which stands for Uncertainty Quantification for Describe Anything, Anywhere, at Any Moment), the system compares multiple descriptions of the same object, seen from different viewpoints, to quantify the robot’s uncertainty about what it saw.  It then selects additional views to reduce the uncertainty and combines these captions into a more accurate description of the object, which it saves to memory. The researchers also employed a special technique to streamline this process so a mobile robot can continually update uncertain memory entries in real time.  When compared to baseline methods, UQ-DAAAM boosted the robot’s confidence and improved the accuracy of its answers to questions about objects, their locations, and when it saw them.  “Contrary to ChatGPT, when we think about physical AI, it is not enough to simply put a disclaimer cautioning that sometimes the robot might be wrong. Allowing a robot to know what it doesn’t know is going to be essential for this technology to be deployed safely and have a positive impact on society,” says Luca Carlone, an associate professor in MIT’s Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AeroAstro), principal investigator in the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems (LIDS), director of the MIT SPARK Laboratory, and the senior author of the paper presenting UQ-DAAAM. He is joined on the paper by co-lead authors and MIT graduate students Harry Zhang and Nicolas Gorlo. The research will be presented at the Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems.  Amending memory This new method builds on the researchers’ prior work, DAAAM, a robot memory system that uses a vision-language model (VLM) to richly describe objects in scenes a robot captures with its onboard cameras. These descriptions are stored as detailed captions in a 3D map-based representation of the robot’s environment that it can call upon later to answer questions.  But the robot sometimes sees objects only partially or from far away, or its camera might capture blurry or poorly lit images. In these cases, DAAAM might describe these objects incorrectly, such as by mistaking a gray chimney for a squirrel perched on a rooftop. “With no way to correct itself, this wrong memory would persist as the robot proceeds in its environment, which could impact downstream applications,” Zhang says. UQ-DAAAM integrates uncertainty quantification into the DAAAM framework. It allows the robot to measure its confidence in the accuracy of object descriptions and fix incorrect captions as it travels through an environment. While on the move, the robot constantly collects and stores images of the world around it. Many of these images show the same objects captured from different angles. UQ-DAAAM uses these additional viewpoints to identify and correct unreliable descriptions. First, it calculates the VLM’s confidence level in the words it generated to describe a potentially mislabeled object. Then, it measures consistency by comparing this description to captions of images that describe the same object from different vantage points. “We fuse both sources of uncertainty into a single number that captures how certain the VLM is in its overall understanding of the object,” Carlone explains. If that number exceeds a certain threshold, the uncertainty is too high, and UQ-DAAAM will refine the caption by using additional images of the object. It does this using a heuristic, or simple rule, that determines which additional viewpoints will reduce the robot’s uncertainty about the object. For instance, it might choose an image captured a few frames later that clearly shows smoke emanating from the chimney.  The researchers mathematically proved that this heuristic can identify the best frames to select without rerunning the VLM, dramatically reducing the amount of computation.  “The key challenge Nico and Harry had to overcome is how to combine VLMs with uncertainty quantification into something that is running in a fraction of a second on a robot that is moving,” Carlone says. Remembering with confidence Once it has identified additional captions that will reduce its uncertainty about the object, the system uses an LLM to fuse them into a single object description. To boost accuracy, the LLM puts more weight on new captions and those with less ambiguity. This refinement step is able to resolve ambiguities for about 92 percent of the objects in the robot’s environment, while only requiring two additional captions per object. It increased the accuracy of object descriptions by 5 percent compared to the state of the art. UQ-DAAAM also provided more accurate answers to questions about the objects it observed, where it saw them, and when it last encountered them than baseline methods. “Performing this uncertainty quantification procedure across the entire map the robot generates allows it to improve its understanding of what it has observed,” Gorlo says. Next, the researchers want to use UQ-DAAAM to guide different types of robots, like mobile robotic manipulators, and apply their uncertainty quantification techniques to other domains.  In addition, they are studying the use of UQ-DAAAM to identify areas of high uncertainty the robot could revisit to improve its understanding of the environment. They are also exploring uncertainty quantification in systems that predict the future state of a robot’s environment. This research is supported, in part, by the U.S. Army Research Laboratory and the U.S. Office of Naval Research. Carlone is currently on sabbatical as an Amazon Scholar; this article describes work performed at MIT and is not associated with Amazon.
2e0612d18143103c: Several staffers at the White House are using computers or mobile devices equipped with residential proxy services that render their internet address available for others to rent, security experts warned today. One of the proxy services is a Russian company whose founder’s web hosting business was ground zero for cyberattacks against election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.

The security firm Layer3 Intel said it detected multiple residential proxy nodes beaconing out from the internet address network reserved for the Executive Office of the President (AS2650). Layer3 said the proxy activity was relatively persistent between October 5 to November 3, and that a review of the proxies available from AS2650 showed they exited from the White House network 236 times during that period.

The proxy tracking company Synthient said on Twitter/X that the activity it saw coming from AS2650 was related to multiple Windows 11 installations of a service called Infatica, a proxy program that is often integrated into “free” mobile and desktop applications. Infatica’s founder Vladimir Fomenko is a Russian man whose hosting firm King Servers was home to six of the eight internet addresses used by Russia’s state security services to compromise databases for election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.
Synthient’s depiction of the outgoing proxy traffic from the dedicated White House network (AS2650). Click to enlarge.

There are dozens of residential proxy providers with varying degrees of legitimacy, many of them based in China or Russia. But at a minimum, they all make it simple for customers to rent someone else’s internet address as a way to anonymize their web traffic or spoof their true location. From a website’s perspective, the traffic from a proxy network user appears to originate from the rented IP address, not from the proxy service customer.
Layer3 Intel said the proxy exit nodes at the White House came from six internet addresses, on 26 of the 30 days, and that most of the activity happens in the evening, between 5 p.m. and midnight.

Incredibly, Infatica was not the only proxy service that reportedly has been reselling access to White House internet addresses: Layer3 Intel said it found 28 separate residential proxy services were able to exit through this network.

“This is public access,” the Layer3 Intel team wrote. “Anybody can obtain it by signing up to a public residential proxy service, paying a few dollars and sending requests through it. We did not selectively target this network or try to make our probes exit from it. We caught this by chance, simply by requesting global rotating access through these services.”
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

As detailed in several stories here over the past year, residential proxy services are a major source of unwanted and often malicious traffic, including account takeover and other cybercrime activity, advertising fraud, and mass content scraping for AI projects.

They can also introduce serious security risks. In late 2025, it was discovered that cybercriminals were mass exploiting a widespread vulnerability in these services that allowed them to probe each proxy endpoint’s local network for vulnerable systems to infect with malware. In January 2026, dozens of proxy services were forced to patch their networks after Synthient Founder Ben Brundage showed how cybercriminals were abusing a vulnerability in these residential proxy services to seize control over devices inside the local networks of unsuspecting users.

“Some of these resellers sell bandwidth for as low as 60 cents a Gigabyte, that means for less than a dollar you can gain access into some of the most confidential and trusted networks,” Brundage told KrebsOnSecurity. “The reseller ecosystem further enables this with any criminal able to buy access while skipping KYC [Know Your Customer] processes.”

All too often, these proxy services are beaconing out from employee devices brought into the workplace. App developers can embed software development kits (SDKs) provided by the residential proxy networks to monetize their software, allowing them to receive a small amount of money on each installation.

As risky as residential proxies can be for unsuspecting end users, they are all too commonly found on government and corporate networks. In a webinar in January 2026, the proxy tracking service Spur found residential proxies in nearly 300 government owned and operated networks, 318 utility companies, 166 healthcare companies or hospitals, and 141 companies in banking and finance. In a blog post earlier this year, the security firm Infoblox said it discovered that fully 65% of its customer base was querying one or more residential proxy related domains.
1c5f8252381c9e95: Menurut ahli falsafah dan sejarawan Perancis yang terkenal, Pierre Nora; terdapat satu hubungan erat antara sejarah dan memori. Akan tetapi Nora menegaskan, dalam banyak keadaan memori adalah lebih utama dan dalam banyak keadaan mengatasi sejarah. Ini kerana memori adalah pencarian kebenaran yang objektif a search for objective truth atau satu himpunan bagaimana ia pernah terjadi, a recollection of how it really was.

Sedangkan sejarah tidak sebebas memori, dan kadangkala perlu dikendala. Ini kerana sejarah selalunya mempunyai aspek ideologi dan boleh dimanipulasi, ideological and manipulative. Idea dan gagasan Nora mengenai pertentangan memori melawan sejarah ini boleh ditemukan dalam banyak karya-karya beliau, antara lain The Present. Nation. Memory; Between Memory and History. Problems of Memory Places; World Celebration of Memory; History as Protection from Politics; dan dalam kerja beliau yang paling masyhur, Places of Memory.

Mengapakah Nora lebih berpihak kepada memori berbanding sejarah, sedang beliau adalah seorang sejarawan? Menurut Nora, beliau pertamanya ingin meluruskan semula sejarah dengan membersihkannya dari fakta tertentu.

Fakta-fakta sejarah ini pada Nora telah dimanipulasi oleh agenda politik dan hanya memori secara kolektif yang dapat membetulkan keadaan ini. Nora dalam kerja-kerja akademiknya menyorot bagaimana gerakan politik, pengukuhan identiti kebangsaan Perancis, dan agenda kelompok tertentu boleh mencemarkan sejarah. Tugas sejarawan sebenarnya adalah memelihara atau melindungi memori ini.

Atas alasan inilah Nora melancarkan gagasan beliau yang dikenali sebagai Places of Memory. Bagaimanapun cabaran untuk meluruskan sejarah dengan mencari memori yang benar ini bukanlah mudah, memandangkan memori itu sendiri terputus, tambahan pula tradisi sendiri akan hancur atau ditinggalkan, dan inovasi mengambil tempat sehingga memori kolektif itu sendiri ikut terjejas. Nora menyatakan, memori yang benar hanya datang dari ruang-tempat memori berjejak memory places atau mnemonic places, yang hadir membentuk ruang memori.

Nora menafsirkan konsep places of memory (lieu de memoire) ini sebagai satu fenomena yang signifikan, terzahir ketara atau tidak ketara, yang mana kerana kenekadan masyarakat atau pengaruh zaman telah membentuk sebagai satu lambang warisan untuk bangsa;

Memori kolektif terbentuk oleh kerana memori berjejak ini yang termanifestasi secara benda, fungsi dan lambang. Memori berjejak dalam bentuk benda misalnya adalah monumen, tugu, memorial, perkabungan, penyanjungan, wajah pada stem atau duit kertas, acara yang bersempenakan memori ini, nama jalan; dan lain-lain. Memori yang terputus memerlukan memori berjejak ini supaya dapat diingat kembali dan sekaligus dimurnikan semula sejarahnya. Sesuatu hanya ‘menjadi sejarah setelah memori berakhir, selagi memori dipugar secara kolektif maka sesuatu itu belum menjadi sejarah meskipun sudah berlaku pada masa lampau’; dalam erti kata lain ‘sejarah akan terus hidup jika terus dikenang’.

Harus diingat, memori berjejak Nora selalu dikelirukan oleh ramai sebagai satu tempat, ini kerana terjemahan suntuk place of memory itu dikait dengan physical place, padahal ia telah kehilangan tempat dan lebih kepada simbol atau tanda, kesan, atau jejak.

Saya selalu mengangankan, atau mencita-citakan agar nama Wan Azizah Wan Ismail terlekat dalam memori Malaysia, di saat beliau masih bernafas dan masih hidup. Beliau memiliki tempat dalam memori negara. Saya khuatir meletakkannya dalam sejarah. Ini kerana seperti mana dilihat oleh Nora, sejarah boleh mengalami pemesongan. Buku sejarah boleh diubah oleh pihak yang menang. Sejarah boleh dipadam. Tetapi memori misalnya tidak boleh dipadam. Yazid bin Muawiyah sebagai contoh cuba memadam sejarah mengenai cucu Rasulullah. Dia gagal. Ini kerana Zaynab al Kubra, puteri Fatimah dan Saidina Ali menghidupkan memori abangnya itu dengan segar dan harum. Ia menjadikan kesyahidan itu sentiasa hidup.

Sejarah telah membuktikan bahawa wanita di alam Melayu bukanlah kelompok yang pasif atau hanya berdiri di belakang kejayaan seseorang pimpinan masyarakat. Antara fakta dari lipatan sejarah alam Melayu, dapat dikenali sosok seorang Permaisuri bernama Pramodawardhana yang bertanggungjawab di belakang Kerajaan Majapahit dan Pembangunan Borobudur yang inklusif. Dari era kesultanan hingga ke zaman perjuangan kemerdekaan dan era pemodenan dan digital masa kini, wanita Melayu telah memainkan peranan yang amat signifikan sebagai pemimpin, diplomat, pendidik, usahawan, pemikir sosiobudaya, dan tiang seri utama dalam keharmonian nusa bangsa.

Di saat berlakunya krisis dalam masyarakat, wanita terbukti menjadi penyelamat. Seperti dilakukan oleh Tengku Ampuan Intan Tengku Alang Hussain yang menjadi Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan antara tahun 1869-1872 iaitu ketika berlakunya pertelingkahan untuk merebut kuasa. Watak sedemikian muncul lagi di zaman kita, dengan nama Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.

Selaku timbalan perdana menteri (2018-2020) dan pemimpin di Kementerian Pembangunan Wanita, Keluarga dan Masyarakat (KPWKM), Wan Azizah ketika itu telah melancarkan Pelan Tindakan Kebangsaan Menangani Punca Perkahwinan Bawah Umur (2020-2025). Pelan ini merangkumi strategi menyeluruh berasaskan lima punca utama yang digariskan menerusi kajian mendalam, iaitu kemiskinan sosioekonomi, kekurangan akses kepada pendidikan, kepincangan maklumat kesihatan reproduktif, kelonggaran undang-undang, serta persepsi dan stigma masyarakat. Saya membayangkan bagaimana kiranya memori Wan Azizah ini disuburkan terus. Dan memori itu diberi nyawa apabila lima punca di atas terus dikaji dan diberi solusi oleh sebuah universiti. Kita ahli akademik mengkaji dan memberi solusi, atas nama Wan Azizah. Berbahagi pahala.

Satu lagi tonggak utama dalam perjuangan pemerkasaan wanita yang sentiasa Wan Azizah tekankan ialah pengiktirafan terhadap golongan suri rumah yang memerlukan perlindungan keselamatan sosial yang sewajarnya. Di tangan beliau lahir program i-Suri dan i-Sayang yang hari ini mesti diteruskan sebagai usaha menangani jurang perlindungan sosial. Kerajaan ketika itu melancarkan Skim i-Suri di bawah Caruman Sukarela Insentif Suri bagi memastikan suri rumah berdaftar dalam sistem eKasih mendapat tabungan hari tua di Kumpulan Wang Simpanan Pekerja (KWSP) dengan bantuan insentif kerajaan.

Memori atau legasi kerja bekas timbalan perdana menteri ini mesti dibaja. Ia mesti diberi, bak kata Pierre Nora, sebuah tanah pamah, sebuah watan dan tekad yang dapat menampang places of memory (lieu de memoire) tersebut. Kalau ada rezeki harapnya memori Wan Azizah ini akan dapat ditegakkan di kala beliau masih hidup, dan di kala saya masih berkhidmat sebagai ahli akademik.
Ini hanyalah angan-angan saya. Agar nama Wan Azizah itu abadi, dan mengatasi sejarah. Ia boleh dan Insya-Allah menjadi memori, satu kenangan yang wangi dan lama. Biarkan ia abadi.

36d4af5b6e476e47: From Clement Stanley
Malaysian Indian People’s Party, a Perikatan Nasional component, decided to skip the Melaka state election as a matter of principle, or so they say.
MIPP president P Punithan said the party would not compromise its principles simply to secure seats in the Nov 14 polls.

MIPP’s struggle, he declares, is to defend the interests of the Indian community with dignity and principles, and “that the community’s voice and interests deserve proper recognition and representation in the political landscape”.
In short, MIPP likely does not want to be seen as token for the opposition coalition’s supposed inclusiveness.
Which, in essence is fine. After all, how can a party market itself as an outfit that champions the Indian cause when it finds itself marginalised?
It is just horrible branding — apart from the fact they lost their deposits in the Johor election — which could be a factor as to why seat negotiations failed.
Yet, MIPP’s dilemma is also, to a certain extent, MIC’s.
What role does MIC play in the bigger scheme of things with respect to its affiliation with Barisan Nasional?
Would MIC be willing to accept the fact that it is by and large irrelevant and a “diversity hire” of sorts?
Are they content being pliant to Umno, BN’s lynchpin, since such an arrangement may guarantee a government post?
Or will they only display bravado, via empty threats to quit BN, before the party’s AGM?
To MIPP’s credit, they were brave to acknowledge where they stand in PN. It is now time for the MIC to do the same.
Pliancy and bravado, however, also bring us to MCA.
Mocked as being Umno’s lapdog for the longest time, MCA leaders walked out of BN’s candidate announcement over seat allocations, also over principles.

The party, its president Wee Ka Siong said, cannot be pushed around and deserves to be treated with dignity. Wee also later called out BN chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi on his claim that talks held after the walkout were “positive”.
Whether one believes it was just “wayang kulit”, the bravado eventually secured three seats for MCA to contest at the Melaka election.
But can MCA consider this a win?
The optics will definitely boost its morale.
Perhaps this will give MCA something to build on. Perhaps they believe that by riding on the tailcoats of a BN-PN pact they will win over more Chinese support for the party.
But truth be told, their victory would be somewhat hollow if they won based on the support of the non-Chinese voters.
Be that as it may, MCA must surely know they are no force to be reckoned with amongst the Chinese electorate.
But, if survival is the name of the game, then by all means be indebted to the Malay support for putting them back in a position of power in Johor, Negeri Sembilan and now very likely, in Melaka.
MCA now need only ask themselves, “How high?” when told to jump by the likes of Umno and PAS.

e0aa4e6ab2afafa9: Dalam tulisan ini saya ingin mengingatkan diri saya dan orang Melayu Islam yang lain supaya menjaga keimanan agar tidak terjebak dengan perkara yang boleh mengancam kedudukan kita di akhirat nanti.
Ini adalah berkaitan dengan suatu kumpulan orang Melayu Islam yang ‘galak’ sangat menghukum dan menuduh orang bukan Islam rakyat Malaysia sebagai kafir, musuh-musuh Islam dan ejen penjajah.

Lebih buruk lagi, kumpulan ini juga tidak terasa apa-apa dosa menuduh orang Islam lain sebagai munafik dan sebagai berkelakuan seperti dajal akhir zaman. Tuduhan liberal dan sesat kepada orang Melayu umat Islam daripada kumpulan itu dah jadi kebiasaan mereka.

Maka itu saya terpanggil untuk memberi peringatan walaupun saya bukan ustaz atau mufti atau profesor bidang Islam dan juga presiden NGO Islam seperti Abim dan Ikram sebabnya ada kebisuan dalam kalangan tersebut, entah kenapa.

Dalam pembacaan semua hadis-hadis koleksi saya seperti Sahih Al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abu Dawud dan Al-Muwatta versi terjemahan Inggeris serta juga At-Tirmidzi, An-Nasa’i dan Ibn Majah versi terjemahan Indonesia, saya terserempak dengan suatu hadis yang pada mulanya suatu misteri tetapi akhirnya menjadi pedoman serta ingatan saya sebagai seorang Muslim yang menjiwakan Sunnah Rasulullah dan bukannya perbuatan atau kata-kata ustaz dan agamawan lain:
Hadis sahih ini juga mengingatkan kita tentang pentingnya amalan dalam menentukan nasib kita di akhirat. Rasulullah SAW bersabda:

"Sesungguhnya, seseorang di antara kalian ada yang beramal dengan amalan ahli neraka sehingga jarak antara dirinya dan neraka tinggal sehasta, lalu takdir mendahuluinya, sehingga ia beramal dengan amalan ahli syurga dan masuklah ia ke dalam syurga. Sebaliknya, seseorang di antara kalian ada yang beramal dengan amalan ahli syurga sehingga jarak antara dirinya dan syurga tinggal sehasta, lalu takdir mendahuluinya, sehingga ia beramal dengan amalan ahli neraka dan masuklah ia ke dalam neraka." (Hadis Riwayat Bukhari dan Muslim)

Pertama sekali saya berdepan hadis ini adalah versi Inggeris dan saya dapat versi Melayu ini dari internet. Saya amat terkejut apabila dikatakan Rasulullah supaya jangan kita anggap seseorang itu yang berkelakuan seperti orang jahat akan berakhir dengan ia ke neraka dan seorang yang berkelakuan seperti orang baik tidak semestinya berakhir dengan ditempatkan di syurga.

Bagi saya, kalau seorang yang berkelakuan tidak bermoral dan berniat jahat itu mungkin di akhir hayatnya akan menjadi baik kerana bertaubat dan membetulkan kesalahannya itu suatu kemungkinan dan suatu harapan baik.

Tetapi, saya terasa pelik bila merenung macam mana seorang yang ‘baik’ bersembahyang, berjuang atas nama Islam, memimpin parti politik Islam setengah abad ada kemungkinan berakhir di tempat selain syurga?

Saya memang tidak menyangka yang pada suatu hari nanti saya akan melihat dengan mata saya sendiri dan mendengar dengan telinga sendiri tokoh-tokoh Melayu umat Islam yang saya amat hormati dan sayangi mengubah kelakuan mereka 180 darjah menjadi orang yang berkelakuan tidak bermoral dan tidak berperasaan kemanusiaan langsung ketika saya dan mereka masih hidup di dunia ini.

Sejak saya kenal sedikit politik sewaktu umur dua puluhan bermula di Amerika Syarikat saya menjadi lebih matang sewaktu era Reformasi tahun 1998 ketika Anwar Ibrahim dipenjarakan, dimalukan dan dipukul separuh mati daripada orang Melayu Islam kita sendiri.

Ketika itu saya melihat institusi agama kesemuanya senyap seribu bahasa dan institusi pengajian tinggi duduk diam saja tak buat apa. Yang membantu Anwar adalah sebuah parti politik yang bertemakan perjuangan reformis Islam dan ia menjadi harapan dan payung saya selama hampir 15 tahun.
Pada saya, semua tokoh-tokoh parti ini memang perlu menjadi sanjungan dan ikutan orang Melayu umat Islam kerana kecekalan dan keikhlasan mereka melawan Umno dan Dr Mahathir Mohamad ketika itu.
Ia adalah Melayu lawan Melayu. Melayu Islam melawan Melayu nasionalis. Saya di dalam golongan Melayu Islam dan membenci Melayu nasionalis.

Walaupun kebencian saya terhadap Umno dan Mahathir amat besar sekali, tidak ada sekali pun saya pernah menuduh mereka itu munafik atau kafir atau menjadi ejen penjajah, jauh sekali sebagai musuh-musuh Islam.
Bagi saya perbalahan adalah kepada mereka yang terperangkap dengan konsep Islam tradisi dan Islam institusi maka reformis Islam perlu membebaskan mereka daripada belenggu tersebut.
Saya masih ingat reformis yang mengikuti reformasi tidak pernah membakar gambar tokoh-tokoh Umno atau menuduh mereka munafik serta mempunyai ciri dajal.
Memanglah ada sejarah seorang tokoh dan suatu parti itu mengkafirkan Umno tetapi saya, walaupun menjadi ahli parti tersebut, tidak pernah bersikap demikian.
Saya amat tergamam apabila saya melihat parti yang memperjuangkan Islam sebagai antiasabiyah atau perkauman tiba-tiba bersekongkol dengan parti yang memperjuangkan perkauman Melayu.

Saya berasa terkejut apabila dari lidah tokoh Melayu Islam sendiri terkeluar kata-kata kesat dan menghina kepada kaum bukan Islam serta menuduh kaum Islam lain sebagai bersahabat dengan musuh-musuh Islam dan penjajah.
Saya amat terkejut juga apabila tergamak ahli parti itu membaca Qunut Nazilah ke atas rakyat Malaysia daripada semua kaum dan agama yang menjadi lawan politik mereka.
Dan kini saya juga terkejut tentang lafaz munafik dan dajal yang dilemparkan kepada orang Melayu umat Islam yang berbeza polisi dan pandangan dalam politik.
Lebih teruk lagi parti itu mengutip derma jihad untuk mengiyakan fitnah jelas ahlinya ke atas orang bukan Islam yang lain demi ‘perjuangan menegakkan Islam’ dalam negara.
Kita semua akan meninggalkan dunia ini di akhir hayat kita. Apakah penjelasan kita bila berdepan dengan penghakiman akhirat nanti?
Adakah kita akan bergantung kepada argumen ‘demi perjuangan Islam’ maka any way is the halal way?
Janganlah kita ghairah sangat bertakbir dan bertempik Islam namun tergadai akhirnya iman dan jiwa kita kepada kemunafikan dan pendajjalan diri kita sendiri di akhir hayat nanti.

a40b144ab5da56eb: From a layperson’s perspective, following the legal back-and-forth in the Malaysian courts can be rather taxing.
It often appears to be a war of words, legal arguments, constitutional interpretations and courtroom strategies, all aimed at persuading the presiding judge or judges.

Beneath the pomp and pageantry inherited from the British legal system, however, lie issues of profound constitutional significance that may or may not affect our lives today, but could have far-reaching consequences for generations to come.

When Malaysia was formed in 1963, several safeguards were negotiated to protect the interests and autonomy of North Borneo (now Sabah). Among these was Point 11 of the Inter-Governmental Committee (IGC) Report, under the heading tariffs and finance.
It provided that “North Borneo should retain control over its own finances, development and tariffs, with the right to formulate its own taxation policies and raise loans on its own credit”.

One can argue that the spirit and substance of this safeguard are found in the constitutional expression of Article 112C of the Federal Constitution, read together with Section 2(1) of Part IV of the Tenth Schedule and Clauses (1), (3) and (4) of Article 112D.

These provisions form the constitutional basis for Sabah's entitlement to a special grant equivalent to two-fifths (40%) of the net revenue derived by the federal government from Sabah, subject to the relevant constitutional provisions.

Former Sabah minister Yap Pak Leong revived the historical significance of this arrangement, maintaining that the 40% revenue-sharing arrangement was a fundamental condition underpinning Sabah's decision to join in the formation of Malaysia.
"Right from the start, I emphasised this share of 2/5 revenue to be a condition for Sabah to become part of Malaysia.”
He further stressed that without this safeguard being enshrined in the Federal Constitution, Sabah would not have agreed to participate in the formation of Malaysia.

The role Sabah and Sarawak played in forming Malaysia must be recognised, unlike the federated states of Malaya. The Borneo states negotiated separate terms under the IGC, one of which is Sabah’s entitlement to 40% revenue sharing of all taxes collected in Sabah.

From what I understand, the federal government is not objecting to Sabah’s right to the 40% revenue sharing, but to the High Court judgment on Oct 17, 2025, in favour of the Sabah Law Society (SLS), directing the federal and state government to commence a review within a stipulated period.

Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim himself promised during the last state election that the government would not appeal the High Court’s decision, but for whatever reasons, it seems he has reneged on that promise to the Sabah people.
On another point, one cannot help but question the position taken by the state government in these proceedings.
Having entered the case as an intervener at a relatively late stage, the state government appears caught between competing legal and political considerations.
Yet, arguably, it should have been at the forefront pursuing Sabah's constitutional entitlement.
The state government possesses the political mandate, institutional authority and constitutional standing to negotiate directly with the federal government.

Rather than allowing the matter to become an extended courtroom battle initiated by SLS on behalf of the people of Sabah, it should be exercising that authority to secure a meaningful and just resolution for Sabah's 47 "lost years".

In another case, another NGO, Sabah Action Body Advocating Rights (Sabar) has taken the federal government to court on February 27, 2025, disputing the validity of the Territorial Sea Act (TSA) 2012, which limits the State's maritime boundary to just three nautical miles.

While the Sabah state government may have its own reasons for not initiating legal challenges regarding Sabah's rights, and Sabahans are not privy to their arguments, it is only fair to ask where the Sabah government stands in relation to these key court challenges.
The position is unlike in Sarawak, where the state government has led similar challenges.

Importantly, after more than six decades since Sabah agreed to become a part of Malaysia, one uncomfortable reality remains: according to official statistics, Sabah continues to record the highest poverty incidence in the country.
That is a sobering indictment of the development gap that persists despite Sabah's immense natural resources and its contributions to the Malaysian federation.
The legal arguments may continue. Appeals may be filed, constitutional provisions may be debated, and lawyers may argue over jurisdiction, procedures and remedies.
But beyond the courtroom, ordinary Sabahans continue to face the realities of poverty, inadequate infrastructure, water and electricity shortages, and limited economic opportunities.

The fundamental question is this: after more than 60 years in the Malaysian federation, should Sabahans still have to fight in court for constitutional assurances that were meant to protect their interests from the very beginning?

The 40% entitlement should not be treated as a political bargaining chip, nor should its fulfilment be reduced to a battle of legal technicalities. It is a constitutional matter rooted in the historical terms and safeguards surrounding the formation of Malaysia.
It is about justice, constitutional accountability and the future of Sabah.
The people of Sabah have waited long enough. Following Lord Hewart CJ’s well-known dictum, “justice must be seen to be done”.

c6b1da594a8a831d: Over 60% of Floridian voters voted to cut property taxes, which has been surging in recent years. AP Photo/Rebecca Blackwell)Many Florida homeowners cheered on Nov. 3, 2026, when more than 60% of voters approved a constitutional amendment to significantly reduce property taxes. Under the measure, Amendment 3, a homeowner’s tax break known as a homestead exemption would go from the current US$51,400 to $150,000 in 2027 and increase again to $250,000 in 2028. By shielding more of a home’s assessed value from taxation, this exemption effectively lowers homeowners’ tax bills. New Florida residents who buy a home would also reportedly be eligible for a property tax break, but on a more phased-in basis. But the measure comes with a hefty price tag. The Florida Legislature’s research arm estimated the measure would reduce annual revenue from property taxes by $11.8 billion. This translates to a 30% reduction in revenue for Florida counties and a 13% cut for smaller municipal governments. While homeowners will get some relief, the budget crunch due to the lower tax revenue will affect other Floridians in more adverse ways. As economists who have been following the debates over Amendment 3, we argue that local governments will struggle to fund basic services with less money. And we expect more sweeping economic consequences as well – including less affordable residential housing and a broader shift of the tax burden away from relatively wealthier homeowners to those who are less well off. How Amendment 3 would work Much of the political momentum for Amendment 3 came from a rise in the cost of living and frustration over rising property taxes. These now average just over $3,000 annually but can run much higher for Floridians with more expensive homes. In addition to raising the homestead tax exemption, Amendment 3 lowers the cap on annual assessments on rental and commercial properties from a 10% increase to a 5% increase. Since property taxes are based on an asset’s assessed value, this language effectively limits but doesn’t rule out tax hikes for businesses. So landlords, for example, could still see meaningful annual tax increases as their properties go up in value – costs that would likely be passed on to renters. Amendment 3 makes clear that school-related property taxes are exempt from these tax cuts. It also lists some theoretical limits on how local governments should use tax dollars, as a way to ensure continued funding for essential services such as public safety, infrastructure or obligations for employee retirement benefits. But it also states that funds may be used for “expenditures approved” by local and county governments – ambiguous wording that suggests these stipulations can be breached. Who pays the bill? Florida property taxes are levied and collected by some 640 local government entities. There’s no state income tax, so any reductions in property tax revenue directly affect local and county governments. With tax revenue slashed, businesses, landlords and owners of other non-homestead properties like second homes would almost certainly see their taxes go up. This is a typical pattern: When governments cut property taxes for some groups, taxes shift to other groups. Essential public services, including fire and police departments, could face sharp budget cuts due to the shortfall from lower property taxes. Orange County Fire Rescue Department via AP This dynamic is likely to play out with local governments as they try to keep revenue stable: Amendment 3 would force them to hike taxes in other areas to make up for the shortfall. This could include increases in state and local sales taxes, an expansion of the list of goods subject to sales taxes, or a hike in “documentary stamp taxes,” which are required on documents such as deeds, bonds and mortgages. State and local governments could also impose higher fees for specific services, such as solid waste treatment and stormwater utilities. Another option is to hike permits and inspection fees, fuel taxes or other service charges such as vehicle registration fees. Finally, local governments could raise tourism-related taxes, such as on food, beverages and hotels. But this recourse wouldn’t help counties with limited tourism, and such revenues fluctuate in any event. In the end, though, essential services would still almost certainly be affected. Funding for police, fire and emergency medical services is primarily the responsibility of local governments, and, for most counties, they make up the largest line item in their annual expenditures. Reducing property taxes would amount to a direct hit, especially in smaller, less-populated counties. And if local governments do raise sales tax rates to the extent they can, lower-income Floridians will bear a disproportionate burden as they spend much more of their income on consumption. They’re also far more likely to rent than own a home, so any increased rents would take a bigger toll. A looming affordable housing crunch? Less noticed in the debate over Amendment 3 was how it would affect the state’s affordable housing shortage. We argue that the structure of the property tax cut will likely create more incentives for counties and developers to build commercial structures instead of more residential housing. When developers build residential homes, they require a basic level of public services to support residents and the local infrastructure. In fact, property taxes in much of Florida effectively subsidize residential home development: For every dollar that a homeowner pays in property taxes, it costs county governments around $1.20 to provide those services. This gap will only grow when property tax revenues fall. From the standpoint of local and county governments, then, it may make more sense to focus on commercial or industrial construction as a way to keep tax revenues stable. But with fewer homes built at the expense of business construction – from manufacturing to data centers – the supply squeeze will only drive up prices and rents for the workers who are needed for those jobs. Now that Amendment 3 is on the books, Florida’s county and local governments will confront major trade-offs. We believe that state officials will come to realize how much of a change has been made – and how quickly their priorities may have to shift. This article has been corrected to note that the current homestead exemption is $51,400 and that new Florida residents who buy a home are eligible for a property tax break on a phased-in basis.
